articles.title: Kyle Schwarber Ties Phillies Record For Most 40-Plus Home Run Seasons
articles.summary: Philadelphia Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber hit his MLB-leading 40th home run Wednesday.
articles.body: Philadelphia Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber hit his MLB-leading 40th home run Wednesday. Schwarber drove a 98-mph fastball off Seattle starter Bryan Woo approximately 425 feet into right-center field, a three-run shot that gave the Phillies a 6-0 lead over the Mariners in the second inning. Schwarber's homer tied a Phillies record for the most 40-plus homer seasons, matching former first baseman Ryan Howard. The 33-year-old Schwarber, who hit 56 homers last season, is also tied for the most 40-plus homer seasons among active players with Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers and Aaron Judge of the New York Yankees. Schwarber's 227 homers with Philadelphia are the second-most in a player's first five seasons with a club. He trails only Babe Ruth, who had 235 homers with the New York Yankees. Schwarber, who spent six years with the Chicago Cubs, has 380 career homers. Matt Olson (Braves) and Yordan Alvarez (Astros) trail Schwarber in homers with 36 each. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé Scores Hat-Trick For Real Madrid In 2nd Match Of LaLiga Season
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappé’s first goals of the season came via a hat-trick in Real Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Real Sociedad on Wednesday.
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé’s first goals of the season came via a hat-trick in Real Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Real Sociedad in the Spanish league on Wednesday. Mbappé scored once in the first half and twice in the second to lead Madrid to its win over Sociedad in Mourinho’s return to the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium. Jude Bellingham had two assists, including on Vinícius’ first goal of the season in the second half. Madrid had opened its Spanish league campaign with a win at Espanyol. Sociedad had lost its league opener at Real Betis.

articles.title: 2026 College Football Playoff Predictions: Will Big Ten's Dominance Come To An End?
articles.summary: FOX Sports' Joel Klatt made his predicitons for Power Four conference champions, 12-team bracket and his national champion.
articles.body: It's about that time, as the offseason winds down, and predictions start looming. Which teams are bound to make waves this college football season? As Oregon returns plenty of production from their 2025 team and Indiana aims for a repeat title, the competition for conference championships and a national title are wide open. Here are Klatt's predictions for every Power Four conference champion, 12-team bracket and his national champion prediction: Conference Championship Game Predictions Big Ten Oregon Defeats Indiana Klatt's thoughts: "I do think that the Big Ten is absolutely loaded at the top. I think all of us know that after all these preseason rankings have finally come out. We saw Ohio State at the top of the AP [Top 25 Poll]. Oregon was at the top of my preseason poll. And you still have Indiana, the defending national champion. You've got teams like USC, Penn State and Michigan, who will all be in there vying and trying to level up into that rarefied air of those top three teams in the Big Ten. "Ohio State's schedule is going to be too difficult. … They've got to play at Iowa after opening on the road in Week 2 against Texas. They've got to play on the road several times against very difficult opponents. They've got to go to USC. They've got to go to Indiana. These are all very difficult places to play. That's why I don't think Ohio State will make it to Indianapolis. "Oregon's also got a difficult schedule, but I think they're going to be prepared to handle it. I think Indiana gets back into that spot. … I'm going to take Dan Lanning and the Ducks." SEC Texas Defeats Georgia Klatt's thoughts: "This is a very deep conference — we all know that. I think there are two, at least in this month, that are maybe better than the rest. We'll see how it plays out, particularly with a team like LSU. But I really, really like Georgia and Texas. I really like Texas a lot. My wild card is LSU. "You start to wonder to yourself if [Texas coach Steve Sarkisian] can get over the hump. Let's just say if Ohio State were to beat them early in the season, that could be a real defining moment for that program. For them to turn things around and break some of those barriers later in the season — one of those barriers being Georgia and Kirby Smart. I don't want to bet against Georgia and Kirby Smart, but I don't know if they're going to have the firepower to keep up with what could be a very good offense in Texas. "I think Texas and Steve Sarkisian can get over that hump." Big 12 Texas Tech Defeats BYU Klatt's thoughts: "This one's pretty easy. Texas Tech is the most talented team in the league, and they've got a pretty soft schedule. They only have one ranked opponent on their schedule as it stands right now: Week 3 against Houston. "Who will Texas Tech face? I like Arizona a lot, but I just don't love their schedule in the Big 12. They've got quarterback Noah Fifita coming back. I really like what they've done with their program. … You just look at these schedules and I just don't love it for Arizona. They've got at BYU, at Texas Tech and home against Utah. "I think the second spot goes to the winner of the Holy War, BYU and Utah. As was the case a year ago, I'm going to lean toward BYU. A lot of turnover at Utah. Meanwhile, BYU, they still have head coach Kelani Sitake, quarterback Bear Bachmaier and running back LJ Martin. "Texas Tech is just at a different level in terms of the roster compilation against the other Big 12 schools." ACC Miami (Fla.) Defeats SMU Klatt's thoughts: "Miami has a similar gap over the ACC. I don't see them losing an ACC game this year. They might lose to Notre Dame. I'll predict that they do lose to Notre Dame. But Miami is not going to have a large issue when it comes to the ACC schedule. "The real question is who is Miami going to face? You start to throw out those teams you think might have the talent and schedule to get themselves into the ACC Championship Game. I have four teams I considered here: Clemson, Virginia Tech, SMU and Louisville. With Clemson and Virginia Tech, I just don't know. … Louisville and SMU happen to play each other in a monster game in September. I'm going to go with SMU because they're 14-2 in ACC play since joining the conference a year ago. "But SMU is not in Miami's hemisphere, at least as it currently stands." The 12-Team Bracket 1.Oregon Ducks Klatt's thoughts: "If Oregon were to win the Big Ten with only one loss, then I think the Ducks take the No. 1 seed. They're rewarded for winning the Big Ten." 2.Notre Dame Fighting Irish Klatt's thoughts: "I think Notre Dame goes undefeated, but their schedule is just not anywhere close to Oregon's." 3.Miami (FL) Hurricanes Klatt's thoughts: "With only one loss to an undefeated Notre Dame on the road, I think Miami gets the No. 3 seed. … They're 12-1 with an ACC championship." 4.Texas Longhorns Klatt's thoughts: "The fourth spot is a tough call. I think it'll come down to a team that did not play in their conference championship game, but beat a conference champion. Texas is going to get the fourth spot because the SEC championship, fresh off a win against Kirby Smart and Georgia, will help give Texas all the love that they want, and they're going to be one spot ahead of a team that beat them: Ohio State." 5.Ohio State Buckeyes Klatt's thoughts: "Ohio State is going to be rated one spot ahead of the sixth-place team, Indiana, because in this prediction, I've got Ohio State with a win over Indiana. Ohio State would have wins over Texas and Indiana, but loses on the final bye seed because Texas has the SEC championship." 6.Indiana Hoosiers Klatt's thoughts: "Indiana would have the sixth seed because of their loss to Ohio State as an 11-2 team." 7.Georgia Bulldogs Klatt's thoughts: "Georgia would be No. 7 after the loss to Texas in the SEC Championship Game." 8.Texas Tech Red Raiders Klatt's thoughts: "Texas Tech's strength of schedule is not anywhere close. So, even as a conference champion, unless they were undefeated and beating everyone by 20 or 25 — I could see them losing a game in the Big 12 slate — I've got them as the eighth seed." 9.USC Trojans Klatt's thoughts: "Now, it starts to get interesting. I think everyone can agree that the first eight teams are the best eight teams. Who in the world is going to play themselves into the final at-large spots? I'm bullish on [USC]. … I think USC is going to have a real fantastic year. I like what they're doing at the line of scrimmage, both offensively and defensively. I love the fact that they're going to run the football. I love the fact that they're returning their starting quarterback. I've got them going 10-2 with loss to Oregon and Indiana, but they pick up a huge resume-building win against Ohio State." 10.LSU Tigers Klatt's thoughts: "I just think LSU is going to come out and play very solid football. That doesn't mean they're going to win their conference. I don't know if they're going to go to that echelon. But I can certainly see them fixing what happened on the offensive side of the football. … Lane Kiffin's going to have them generating 500 yards of offense, week in and week out. This idea that it's somehow a question or anomaly of how this is going to come together with all these players from the transfer portal, let's not act like Kiffin hasn't done this before. … LSU is going to be a 10-2 team." 11.Alabama Crimson Tide Klatt's thoughts: "I've got three teams going for the final at-large spot in the College Football Playoff: Penn State (they're going to be 10-2), Alabama (at 10-2) and the winner of the Michigan-Oklahoma game. I think the winner of that game will go 9-3. So, they're going to have a huge resume-building win out of conference, but they're still 9-3. … I think Penn State gets thrown out right away because they won't have a resume-building win. In this scenario, they would have lost to Michigan and USC and there's not a marquee win on their schedule. Alabama would be 10-2 against either 9-3 Michigan or Oklahoma. "This team should be excellent on defense. … This is a team that I think can get back to that Alabama defensive identity." 12.Boise State Broncos Klatt's thoughts: "Let's just go with Boise State. Can anyone predict the Group of 5? These rosters turn over with such a huge degree. … I think Boise State will get rewarded with a tougher strength of schedule." First Round No. 5 Ohio State Defeats No. 12 Boise State Klatt's thoughts: "Ohio State should win this game pretty handily." No. 6 Indiana Defeats No. 12 Boise State Klatt's thoughts: "Kalen DeBoer and company go up to Bloomington and guess what? They still can't stop Indiana from running the football. Indiana might run it 55 times in the weather up there." No. 7 Georgia Defeats No. 10 LSU Klatt's thoughts: "Great year for Lane Kiffin. I do think they need to win a playoff game for them to reach their expectations. … But Georgia moves on." No. 9 USC Defeats No. 8 Texas Tech Klatt's thoughts: "I don't think Texas Tech, based on what we saw last year in the postseason when it got shut out by Oregon, will be up to par with a team like USC, who'll be very tested by that point." Quarterfinals No. 1 Oregon Defeats No. 9 USC Klatt's thoughts: "I like USC a lot, but not in this game. Oregon's my No. 1 overall seed for a reason." No. 2 Notre Dame Defeats No. 7 Georgia Klatt's thoughts: "I think Notre Dame is going to be incredible. They're going to play against Georgia, and they're going to win. Notre Dame is going to win that game for the second time in three years." No. 3 Miami Defeats No. 6 Indiana Klatt's thoughts: "I thought it was a coin flip… but Miami is just building something. I think Miami wins that game." No. 5 Ohio State Defeats No. 3 Texas Klatt's thoughts: "This would be the fourth meeting in the last three years. I have to take Ohio State. I think they have something over Texas." Semifinals No. 1 Oregon Defeats No. 5 Ohio State Klatt's thoughts: "I said that Oregon is super talented… at this point, who knows what the depth looks like for Ohio State?… Give me Oregon." No. 2 Notre Dame Defeats No. 3 Miami Klatt's thoughts: "A rematch of that game in South Bend this year. I think Notre Dame wins the first one, I think Notre Dame wins the second one. Notre Dame is that good." National Championship No. 2 Notre Dame Defeats No. 1 Oregon Klatt's thoughts: "It might be a curse to be the team that I pick as the national champ. Last year, I picked Clemson. "My national champ in my very first bracket prediction of the year is [drumroll please]: the Notre Dame Fighting Irish."

articles.title: El balón que volvió a salvar a Sandro Rodríguez
articles.standfirst: El campeón del Open de España y Carlos Calvo, presidente de la Federación Española de Footgolf acercan las claves de un deporte que gana terreno
articles.summary: El campeón del Open de España y Carlos Calvo, presidente de la Federación Española de Footgolf acercan las claves de un deporte que gana terreno
articles.body: El balón sigue siendo el mismo compañero de viaje, pero prácticamente todo lo demás cambia. No hay porterías, tampoco compañeros a los que buscar con un pase, ni un rival al que superar. Hay calles, hoyos, desniveles, viento y una distancia que recorrer con el menor número de golpes posible. El Footgolf conserva el gesto más reconocible del fútbol, golpear un balón con el pie, y lo traslada a un escenario completamente diferente. A los 29 años, una lesión de rodilla alejó al exfutbolista tinerfeño Sandro Rodríguez de los estadios. "Pensaba jugar hasta los 36 y no pude hacerlo. Entonces apareció el Footgolf", explica el exjugador del Chennai City. Ha sido tres veces campeón del España, cuatro de Canarias y quedó quinto en el Mundial de México en Mayo de estre año. Hoy defiende su corona en un Open de España que tendrá del 3 al 6 de septiembre en Cádiz y que reunirá a algunos de los mejores jugadores del mundo. "Es una fusión de fútbol y golf que tiene más que ver con el golf, aunque la ejecución se haga con las piernas y los pies", explica Carlos Calvo, presidente de la Federación Española de Footgolf y también jugador. Una combinación que puede parecer sencilla desde fuera, especialmente para quien ha pasado media vida con un balón pegado a los pies. Nada más lejos de la realidad. Sandro Rodríguez lo sabe bien. El exfutbolista del Tenerife y la UD Las Palmas encontró en el Footgolf una segunda vida deportiva después de que la pandemia y unas molestias en una antigua lesión de rodilla precipitaran el final de su etapa en el fútbol. "Me encontraba en India jugando, pero se me empezó a complicar por unas molestias en la rodilla que me impedían estar al cien por cien. Entre una cosa y otra decidí dejarlo y volver a casa", recuerda. Entonces apareció el Footgolf. "Me dio la oportunidad de volver a disfrutar con un balón en los pies, aunque de una manera muy diferente. Sabía que se me podía dar bien, pero no esperaba que tanto y tan rápido. Pronto me di cuenta de que podía competir por ganar torneos", relata con orgullo. Su pasado como futbolista ayudaba, pero no llevaba incorporado ningún atajo hacia el éxito. "Debes estar concentrado desde el hoyo uno al dieciocho", cuenta Sandro. En este sentido, Calvo advierte que "haber jugado al fútbol no te garantiza nada para hacerlo bien en Footgolf". La explicación está en todo aquello que sucede después del golpeo. "En el fútbol siempre hay un compañero que recibe el balón. Aquí estás tú solo ante la naturaleza: pendientes, inclinaciones, subidas, bajadas, viento…", explica el presidente. Sandro coincide y desmonta una de las imágenes que pueden generar las redes sociales: "De sencillo no tiene nada. Evidentemente, en redes casi todos los vídeos que se ven son haciendo un gran golpe y metiéndola en el hoyo, pero desgraciadamente no siempre es así". La técnica importa. La lectura del terreno también. Pero existe un tercer componente que ambos sitúan casi por encima del resto: la cabeza. "Hay que tener una parte mental muy fuerte", señala Calvo. "Cuando estás bien vas tú solo, pero cuando estás mal también. En un deporte colectivo, si tienes un mal día, están tus compañeros para ayudarte y salvarte. Aquí eres tú solo y tienes que afrontarlo". La preparación también desmonta otro tópico. Sandro trabaja en el gimnasio y busca campos de fútbol o pistas de fútbol sala para mantener el golpeo. "Quizás podría compararse con la presión de tirar un penalti", señala. Posiblemente ahí se encuentre una de las razones por las que el Footgolf consigue atrapar a quienes dejan atrás el fútbol profesional. El balón continúa presente y también la competición, pero desaparecen buena parte del desgaste y las exigencias físicas de sus anteriores carreras. Para Sandro, volver a sentir ese contacto fue precisamente una "válvula de escape". "Seguir en contacto con un balón para alguien que ha sido futbolista durante casi toda su vida es importante. Creo que todo deporte que tenga de por medio una pelota atrae demasiado". Calvo lo observa continuamente: "Una vez entran es difícil salir, porque vuelven a competir de cierta manera. No es tan exigente ni tan lesivo como el fútbol. Poder competir en un deporte similar a lo que has hecho durante tantos años es lo que hace que muchos futbolistas puedan entrar". Mientras aumenta el nivel dentro del campo, el Footgolf español libra otra competición fuera de él: crecer, ganar visibilidad y conseguir estructuras cada vez más profesionales. "Está creciendo bastante. Hemos introducido más profesionalismo a la hora de celebrar los torneos, en la decoración y en aspectos en los que antes no hacíamos tanto hincapié", explica Calvo. Sin embargo, evita hablar todavía de consolidación. "Queda mucho. Estamos en una fase de crecimiento y tenemos que seguir trabajando para que algún día pueda ser profesional de verdad". En los últimos tres años, según el presidente, ha aumentado tanto el número de campos como su calidad y también "ha mejorado muchísimo" el nivel de los jugadores nacionales. Pero existe un problema básico para continuar extendiendo el deporte: poder practicarlo cerca de casa. "Necesitamos muchos más campos de Footgolf habilitados en campos de golf. No es lo mismo tener uno a 80 kilómetros que tenerlo a diez o quince minutos", señala. Calvo utiliza el pádel como espejo: su enorme accesibilidad ha facilitado su expansión. "La gente juega mucho al pádel porque en cada esquina hay una pista". Practicar Footgolf, asegura, tampoco requiere un gran desembolso. "Una partida o un entrenamiento son unos 18, 20 o 25 euros. Estás tres o cuatro horas en un campo, en la naturaleza, aislado de la vida y disfrutando de esa paz y tranquilidad". El problema económico aparece principalmente cuando llega la competición: desplazamientos, hoteles y varios días fuera de casa incrementan considerablemente el coste para los jugadores. Para crecer también hace falta que el deporte se vea. Y ahí apareció una ventana especialmente importante con la llegada del Footgolf a la plataforma de DAZN, donde la pasada edición del Open de España quedó plasmada en una producción de casi una hora. "Para nosotros es muy importante entrar en una plataforma que nos pueda dar visibilidad, para que la gente vea el deporte, lo conozca y sepa cómo funciona", reconoce Calvo. "Cuando DAZN aceptó meternos en su plataforma fue una alegría muy grande. Esperemos que pueda ser el inicio de algo muy bonito e impactante para el deporte". La visibilidad sirve, además, para romper prejuicios. Porque detrás de los golpes espectaculares y los hoyos que circulan por las redes hay estrategia, técnica, preparación y muchas horas de competición. Una realidad que Sandro conoce especialmente bien después de una adaptación mucho más rápida de la que él mismo había imaginado: "He sido tres veces Campeón de España y cuatro veces de Canarias. En mayo quedé quinto en el Mundial de México. Se me da bastante bien, la verdad". Todo ese crecimiento tendrá uno de sus principales escaparates del 3 al 6 de septiembre en Cádiz. El Open de España reunirá, a falta del cierre definitivo de inscripciones, a 153 jugadores, con la posibilidad de alcanzar aproximadamente los 155 participantes. "Son bastantes jugadores en un año en el que ha habido un Mundial de por medio y la gente se ha gastado mucho dinero", valora Calvo. El objetivo no es únicamente reunir a los mejores, sino conseguir que quienes viajen hasta Cádiz encuentren un torneo cada vez más cercano a los estándares profesionales que persigue la organización. Incluso la naturaleza jugará su propia partida. "El único hándicap que tenemos, al estar en Cádiz, es el viento. Esperemos que este año no haga el viento extremo de la edición pasada", bromea el presidente, que desea que los participantes encuentren "uno de los mejores torneos que puedan disputar durante el año". Entre los participantes aparecen nombres como Piero Menor o Noé Cortiñas, además de figuras internacionales como Florian Warsemann, reciente campeón del mundo; Gonzalo Novosad, subcampeón mundial; y Matías Perrone, campeón del mundo en 2018 y una de las grandes referencias históricas de la disciplina. Carlos Calvo afrontará el Open desde una posición peculiar. Es presidente, organizador y jugador. Quiere ganar, pero sabe que durante esos días su marcador particular no será únicamente el de su tarjeta. "Soy el primero que quiere ganar. El fútbol nos enseña desde pequeños a ser competitivos", admite. Pero inmediatamente coloca otra victoria por encima: "Si lo que más feliz me hiciera fuera ganar torneos, no podría estar aquí de presidente. A mí me da mucha más satisfacción ver a la gente feliz y que se vaya contenta a casa que ganar yo". Detrás existe todavía una estructura sostenida en buena medida por quienes empujan el deporte por pasión. "Nadie cobra por hacer esto. Lo hacemos por amor al arte", reconoce. Precisamente por eso, el gran objetivo va mucho más allá de llenar campos o aumentar participantes. Cuando mira cinco años hacia delante, Calvo no duda: "Lo que queremos todos es que sea un deporte reconocido. Sabemos que no es fácil crear un deporte nuevo". El Footgolf vive todavía entre los dos mundos nacientes. "Está el golf porque jugamos en sus campos y el fútbol porque forma parte del Footgolf", resume el presidente. Pero la aspiración es conseguir algún día una identidad plenamente reconocida. Mientras ese momento llega, seguirá creciendo golpe a golpe. Con futbolistas que encuentran una segunda competición, jugadores que llegan sin haber pisado antes un vestuario profesional y un Open de España que quiere convertirse en su gran escaparate. El balón sigue rodando. Solo ha cambiado el fin: ahora, en lugar de buscar la portería, busca un hoyo.

articles.title: Police investigating alleged assault in Carse incident
articles.summary: An incident during which Brydon Carse was handcuffed is being investigated by Derbyshire Police, who say they are looking into allegations of assault.
articles.body:
An incident during which England bowler Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub is being investigated by Derbyshire Police, who say they are looking into allegations of assault.

Images circulating on social media on Sunday showed Carse in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers while the pace bowler was on a night out in Derby on Saturday.

The 31-year-old was briefly arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said the incident would be investigated by the Cricket Regulator and, as a result, Carse was removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan.

On Monday, Derbyshire Police said a man had been briefly detained outside Molly Malone's bar, before being released.

"A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night," said the police.

"However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area."

On Wednesday, the police gave a further statement, which said: "We are investigating allegations of an assault in Derby city centre.

"No arrests have yet been made and the investigation is ongoing."

Carse has been approached for a response, while the ECB has not commented.

articles.title: Liverpool’s next mega-money transfer teased after Fabrizio Romano drops “here we go”
articles.summary: Tottenham have been handed some encouragement in the window, with Liverpool having reached a verbal agreement to sign Bradley Barcola.Fabrizio Romano confirm...
articles.body:
Tottenham have been handed some encouragement in the window, with Liverpool having reached a verbal agreement to sign Bradley Barcola .

Fabrizio Romano confirmed on X (formerly Twitter) that the Reds are set to exchange documents in the next 24 hours.

With Spurs' hopes of landing Cody Gakpo this summer reportedly tied to the arrival of one (perhaps even two) forwards ahead of the September 1 deadline , the Dutchman may yet be inching towards the exit door.

Bradley Barcola transfer may pave the way for Cody Gakpo exit

Graeme Bailey at TEAMtalk notes that Andoni Iraola is understood to be "reluctant" to allow the Dutch international to leave in the current window.

An understandable position, if Liverpool only intend to add a right-sided winger to their setup and neglect the need for a backup striker.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

However, reporting from Sky Sports indicates that the Merseysiders would prefer to add a third body to their forward line this summer, which would then surely allow Gakpo to depart in the same window.

If we're comparing the potential sale of Cody Gakpo to Manchester City 's recent £85m package deal with Tottenham for Savio, you'd have to argue that the former should be in a similar ballpark.

The former PSV star has far more readily demonstrated his suitability for life in the English top-flight.

Not to mention the fact that he's proven more than competitive when paired with a fellow left-winger he can rotate alongside.

The argument for keeping Gakpo at Liverpool

We'd be far from comfortable parting ways with a player Iraola appreciates as a possible option for the number nine position.

We have to accept that Alexander Isak cannot be relied upon for every single game this season – particularly not if we intend to challenge on all four fronts.

There's going to be a need for rotation, and the answer can't simply be to allow Liverpool's goal threat to nosedive off a cliff when the Sweden international is being rested.

Not to suggest that Cody Gakpo is necessarily the perfect answer here, but if we're not intending to find a solution in the market, he's probably the best answer we've got at this point in time.

articles.title: Liverpool agree huge fee with PSG for France winger Bradley Barcola
articles.summary: Barcola is poised to join Liverpool in a transfer worth at least £100m
articles.body:
Liverpool have reached an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola .

The Champions League winners have accepted an approach which will guarantee them just over £100m and, including add-ons, could rise to £120m.

The deal is not done yet but Liverpool reached a breakthrough in negotiations after coveting the France winger all summer.

Barcola is poised to become the second most expensive player in Liverpool's history, after Alexander Isak joined last summer for £125m .

However, his price will be significantly lower than the £145m which PSG had been asking for, with Liverpool getting their way in talks.

Barcola's arrival comes as part of Liverpool's long search for a successor to Mohamed Salah , who left on a free transfer and subsequently joined Trabzonspor , though the Frenchman has played more on the left flank.

They had submitted a €100m offer for Yan Diomande , but the Ivory Coast winger also became a target for Paris Saint-Germain , only to overlook both clubs and join Real Madrid instead.

Liverpool also made offers of first £50m and £60m for Yankuba Minteh of Brighton and had also considered Crystal Palace 's Ismaila Sarr .

Barcola is likely to become Liverpool's third summer signing after Jeremy Jacquet , whose move from Rennes was arranged in January, and Victor Munoz , a winger head coach Andoni Iraola wanted.

PSG have already replaced Barcola after bringing in three forwards this summer, in World Cup winner Ferran Torres , Magnes Akliouche and Mika Godts .

Barcola, who only had two years left on his contract at Parc des Princes, had also attracted interest from Arsenal .

articles.title: Paul Sullivan: Cubs’ 150th anniversary team forgets some names that made the franchise unique
articles.summary: CHICAGO — The Chicago Cubs on Monday announced their 150th anniversary team, which includes the usual suspects and some curious omissions. Suffice to say it’...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — The Chicago Cubs on Monday announced their 150th anniversary team, which includes the usual suspects and some curious omissions.

Suffice to say it's not a true representation of 150 years of the franchise, considering few of the fans who voted probably watched anyone from 1876-1975, the first century of Cubs baseball.

It would've been better left to Cubs historians, but because Ed Hartig is the only one they have, Cubs management probably didn't want to put all the responsibility on him.

While the Cubs limited the ballot to players and managers, obviously there's much more to the team's storied history than the 40 players and three managers selected. Many others left their mark on the franchise, including owners, executives, announcers, fans and bar owners.

As the Cubs writer with the longest tenure, dating to 1987, it's my honor to present the real 150th anniversary crew.

Though he posted a 127-158 record in 1982-83, the former Cubs manager famously declared: "Eighty-five percent of the (expletive) world's working. The other 15 come out here. A (expletive) playground for the (expletives). Rip them (expletives). Rip them (expletives), like the (expletive) players." Elia's legend never will dim.

The Granddaddy of Bums was a bleacher staple for decades, destroying the eardrums of several generations of Cubs fans. The Chicago Sun-Times once declared Ronnie Woo dead, only for the Chicago Tribune to locate him at his job delivering pizzas. He entered the newsroom with a half-dozen pizzas yelling: "I'm alive, woo! I'm alive, woo!" He's still alive and wooing.

Bartman earned the respect of Cubdom by refusing to cash in on his sudden fame from the foul ball he deflected during the fateful Cubs collapse in Game 6 of the 2003 National League Championship Series. Rewarded with a 2016 World Series ring for his troubles, Bartman has avoided the media for 23 years and counting.

He kept lights out of Wrigley Field and paid for newspaper ads with a personal letter lambasting a "Dump Durocher clique" of players who wanted manager Leo Durocher ousted.

In July 1892, the Cubs outfielder punched Chicago Evening News writer George Bechel several times for a harsh article about him. The Tribune reported Ryan "assaulted the reporter, using him up pretty badly, cutting a gash in his chin and bruising his face considerably."

Curse maker: William 'Billy Goat' Sianis

The bar owner placed the famous "Billy Goat Curse" on the Cubs for not allowing his goat into the 1945 World Series. It became one of the great legends in sports history. The legend gained greater renown thanks to his nephew, Sam Sianis, who spread the word into the 21st century.

Hired by Tribune Co. to wear hot pants and bring cheesecake to the ballpark, Collins was then fired in 1986 for appearing nude in Playboy. "That's the best thing I've seen out of uniform all year," Harry Caray quipped. Thirty years later, pitcher Jake Arrieta appeared nude in ESPN the Magazine. He was not fired.

He invented the Cubs Convention and celebrity guest conductors for the seventh-inning stretch. Some insist he invented Sammy Sosa, who attracted millions of fans to watch some bad teams.

Cubs fans were usually fully krausened by the third inning before 1988, when the team stopped vendors from selling beer in the bleachers, forcing people to actually get up.

He won three division titles in the 2000s and changed the Cubs' narrative until Tribune Co. stopped spending before selling the team.

He built a championship team from the bottom up and also spent some quality time in the bleacher basket during a bacchanalia before leaving Chicago for good.

Invited by Cubs brass to remove the Curse of the Billy Goat before Game 1 of the 2008 playoffs, he then outed the executives after President Crane Kenney claimed Greanias had invited himself for playoff tickets.

The Elmwood Park native has been sitting on the corner of Waveland and Kenmore avenues during home games since 1958, waiting for baseballs to clear the park with his ballhawk brethren. Few balls now leave the yard since the addition of the video board. "The steroid era was very good for the ballhawks," Mullins once declared.

The old-school rooftop owner still is fighting the Cubs in court over rooftop rights and has been a thorn in the Ricketts family's side for decades.

The late, great owner of Murphy's Bleachers fought the Cubs efforts to block the rooftop owners' views while making Murphy's into a must-stop bar for pregame and postgame fans.

Pitcher Carlos Zambrano, who didn't make the official 150th-anniversary team, deserves his own special category. He sent teammate Michael Barrett to the hospital with a punch and destroyed many a Gatorade dispenser and water cooler. A temperamental, home-run-hitting pitcher with All-Star credentials, Big Z had more character than anyone in the game today.

Sure, Harry Caray was more beloved. But no one broadcast more Cubs losses than Brickhouse, who uttered, "Oh, brother," for most of my childhood.

And the Hall of Famer is still going strong.

He invented the Arne hat shot, made Marla Collins famous and was frequently mentioned during broadcasts by Harry Caray: "Hey, Arne, wouldja look at that!"

Yosh's Gilligan hat was in the Hall of Fame. Enough said about "the king of Wrigley Field."

After the six-fingered reliever belly-bumped an umpire, manager Dusty Baker called it "assault with a deadly belly."

Oddball pitcher: (tie) Bill Faul and Turk Wendell

Faul was the pitcher who once hypnotized his arm, and Wendell brushed his teeth in the dugout.

The elderly gentleman was part of a shake-up by clueless Cubs management during an 8-31 slump in September 1999. Sandke lamented that his bosses told him he "needed some fresh air" and moved him from his position. After some bad newspaper publicity, Sandke was returned to his elevator.

He created the modern-day bleachers in 1937, planting the iconic ivy. Veeck spent his final years sitting in the bleachers with his friends, retelling old stories to the next generation of Cubs fans.

Unanimous selection. No one is really close.

He updates balls and strikes on the old scoreboard before the plate umpire finishes his call and is still the best in the business.

As the only World Series MVP in Cubs history, Zobrist was a logical choice.

When the Cubs demolished the classic doughnut shop for renovations, they changed Wrigleyville forever. Fast-food joints and bars catering to the bro culture now dominate the neighborhood. Thanks, Cubs.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap in club-record deal
articles.summary: Liam Delap has joined Nottingham Forest after being told he was not part of Xabi Alonso’s plans at Chelsea
articles.body:
Liam Delap has completed a move to Nottingham Forest from Chelsea in a club-record deal worth £45m.

The 23-year-old forward has agreed a five-year contract at the City Ground, with Forest becoming his third team in three seasons after being informed he did not feature in Xabi Alonso's plans at Stamford Bridge.

However, newly appointed Forest manager Oliver Glasner made securing the striker a priority during the current transfer window.

"I really can't wait to get started, this is a massive club with a big history," Delap said.

"I spoke to the manager and I like his way, I think he can be the one to really help me develop and make that next step and hopefully I can bring goals here.

"I can't wait to hear the noise at The City Ground and have the fans on my side because I know how loud and important they are.

"As a team we can build something really strong and the main aim is to challenge and be a top club in the Premier League."

The former England youth international had been required to train away from the first team at Chelsea , while his number nine shirt was handed to Joao Pedro after Alonso made his position clear.

Chelsea have secured a profit on a player purchased for £30m from Ipswich 12 months ago, despite him scoring just twice across all competitions last season.

The transfer was completed in time for Delap to potentially debut against Liverpool on Saturday, though it remains unclear if Glasner will place him immediately into his starting line-up.

Forest have endured a difficult start to the season, losing 1-0 at home to Leeds in their Premier League opener before suffering a 2-0 defeat by the same side in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.

Glasner will hope Delap can bring the much-needed firepower to propel Forest up the table this season.

Meanwhile, it could be a busy end to the transfer window for Chelsea as they weigh up a move for wantaway Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez .

Delap is unlikely to be their final sale either, as Enzo Fernandez remains heavily linked with a switch to Manchester City .

articles.title: Police probe ‘assault allegations’ in cricketer Carse-linked incident
articles.summary: Unclear whether England cricketer Brydon Carse had a role in the alleged assault being investigated by police.
articles.body:
Police in Derbyshire are looking into “allegations of assault” following the incident that saw England fast bowler Brydon Carse handcuffed outside a nightclub at the weekend.

Carse was dropped from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan, which begins at Lord’s on Thursday, after the Cricket Regulator initiated an investigation into the incident that saw the Durham paceman arrested outside a late-night bar in Derby – then released after agreeing to leave the scene.

In an updated statement issued late Wednesday, Derbyshire Police said: “We are investigating allegations of assault in Derby city centre. No arrests have yet been made and the investigation is ongoing”.

Further details are unknown, with no clarity over what part – if any – Carse had in the alleged assault. The England and Wales Cricket Board has yet to comment publicly on the latest developments.

An initial statement from the force, released after video of Carse apparently being detained by officers in the street, had said: “A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night. However, the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards, having agreed to leave the area.”

Former England captain Ben Stokes and centrally contracted seamer Matthew Potts both appeared in the video taken in the aftermath of their Durham side’s County Championship victory over Derbyshire, though there is no suggestion either was involved in anything untoward.

Stokes’s successor as Test skipper, Joe Root, spoke angrily on Tuesday about the latest in a growing list of alcohol-related incidents in the England set-up.

Root, who abolished the midnight curfew that contributed to Stokes’s exit following another controversial night out earlier this season, said: “If I’m being brutally honest, I’m really hacked off.

“I’ve spoken to Brydon and when I first found out, my first concern was him as a person. I don’t think I’m speaking out of turn in saying he’s very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions.”

Root added: “But it’s not the isolated incident itself; it’s the fact we continuously keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it’s detracting from what we are doing on the field.”

articles.title: Kenya’s world record holder Sawe withdraws from Berlin Marathon
articles.summary: An undisclosed injury has forced Sebastian Sawe to withdraw from next month’s Berlin Marathon.
articles.body:
World record holder Sebastian Sawe, the first man to break the mythical two-hour barrier in marathons , has pulled out of next month’s Berlin Marathon because of injury, he announced.

The Berlin race, which will take place on September 27, was due to be Sawe’s first outing since April when he broke the two-hour barrier with a run of 1:59:30 to win the London Marathon.

“It is with a heavy heart that I must inform you that I am forced to withdraw from the Berlin Marathon due to injury,” the 31-year-old Kenyan wrote on Instagram on Thursday, but did not specify the nature of his injury.

“I had been looking forward to achieving something special on the streets of Berlin.”

The very flat course has made Berlin a favourite for potential records.

Sawe won the 2025 edition in Berlin with a time of 2:02:16 despite the heat and humidity and the fact he found himself alone at the front without a pacemaker from the 24th kilometre onward.

His world record could be under threat on December 6, with Ethiopian runner Yomif Kejelcha set to compete in the Valencia Marathon, which is also known as a very fast course.

Kejelcha was the second man to run a marathon in less than two hours, finishing 11 seconds behind Sawe in London, and on Sunday broke the world half-marathon record in 56:51.

Upon his return from his record-breaking race in London, Sawe received a hero’s welcome home in Kenya, with fans thronging the airport in Nairobi and the country’s president giving him cash and a car.

articles.title: Predicting WWE's Top Stars in 2030
articles.summary: Right now, there is a negative connotation surrounding WWE due to lackluster storytelling, mismanaged character development, and week-to-week inconsistency on both Raw and SmackDown.
articles.body:
Right now, there is a negative connotation surrounding WWE due to lackluster storytelling, mismanaged character development, and week-to-week inconsistency on both Raw and SmackDown.

Wrestling fans are down on WWE, but that doesn't mean the company can't turn it around by utilizing its current roster of elite performers properly. Despite the glaring issues plaguing Triple H and WWE Creative, there are several marquee names who could help the company out of purgatory.

Here are the WWE Superstars poised to help the brand return to prominence in the coming years.

The most obvious options for cornerstones of the company moving forward would be Oba Femi and Rhea Ripley.

Femi is 28 years old and will turn 32 in 2030. He has already held the NXT Championship twice, beaten Brock Lesnar on two occasions and established himself as one of WWE's most physically imposing performers.

By 2030, he'll be entering what could be the prime of his career, with ample time until then to develop his promo work, character and storytelling.

As for Ripley, she will turn 34 in October 2030, making her one of WWE's most established stars while still in her prime. She already has championship success, a distinctive character and enormous fan recognition, so she should remain the top dog for the foreseeable future.

With Femi being the future monster WWE can build around and Ripley being the established Superstar who should still be there when the next generation arrives, these are WWE's safest bets for top stars in 2030.

Future Faces of WWE: Trick Williams and Tiffany Stratton

While Femi and Ripley are obvious answers, two up-and-coming Superstars on the cusp of greatness are Trick Williams and Tiffany Stratton.

Williams will turn 36 in 2030, but don't let his age fool you; his combination of being newer to the business and the longer shelf life of wrestlers—i.e., John Cena, Roman Reigns, and Cody Rhodes—will make him a long-term asset.

Add in his unique combination of freak athleticism and unquestionable charisma, and he should continue to be involved in major championship-level programs for the next decade.

Stratton will turn 31 in 2030, making it a smart choice to continue her ascent over the next several years. She's already been trusted with major programs and championship opportunities, and her character, athleticism and presentation are positioning her to evolve from a young star with upside into the centerpiece of the women's division.

Williams and Stratton are already a focal point on weekly programming, so another half-decade of experience will only help them climb the ranks of importance in WWE.

Future Main Event Players: Bron Breakker and Roxanne Perez

Two fresh faces who are continuing to prove their worth to WWE every week are Bron Breakker and Roxanne Perez, both of whom are ascending to the top of the card with each passing day.

Breakker will be 33 in October 2030, an ideal age for a main event Superstar who theoretically would have years of main roster experience by then.

Using his explosive athleticism and a believable intensity, he is already heading toward a major showdown with Femi, a potential glimpse at two future pillars of the company colliding.

Perez will be 29 in November 2030, making her a clear choice to become a cornerstone of the WWE Women's Championship picture for many years.

As a former NXT women's champion and already established on the main roster, she could enter her late-20s as one of the division's veterans with world title experience despite still being extremely young.

Breakker and Perez have a ton left to prove on the main roster, but with the proper character development and consistency in the ring, both are poised to become main-event players for a long time.

Potential Breakout Stars: Je'Von Evans and Sol Ruca

For WWE fans looking for Superstars further down the card who could eventually morph into performers worthy of being considered a cornerstone worth building around, look no further than Je'Von Evans and Sol Ruca.

Evans is only 22 years old and will be 26 in 2030. His athleticism and high-energy style have already made him popular in NXT and on the main roster, but if he improves his promos, character and match psychology, he could become a world champion with more experience.

Ruca will turn 31 in August 2030, giving Triple H and WWE Creative every reason to invest early and often in her future.

So far, she has showcased the physical tools and looks to be a top star, but the next four years should be about improving her character and promo work, which would make her an ideal performer to build a division around.

It may be a longer shot that Evans and Ruca rise through the ranks before 2030 to sit atop their respective divisions, but with youth on their side, they are safe bets to keep climbing the ladder to the main event scene.

articles.title: Backstage WWE and AEW Rumors on AJ Lee, Kairi Sane and More
articles.summary: Women's wrestling takes center stage in this collection of pro wrestling rumors, with the latest on former champions AJ Lee, Kairi Sane, and Bayley at the center of insider reports.
articles.body:
Women's wrestling takes center stage in this collection of pro wrestling rumors, with the latest on former champions AJ Lee, Kairi Sane, and Bayley at the center of insider reports.

Dive deeper into each and find out what the future may hold for all three now, thanks to the most trusted reporters in the industry.

AJ Lee last competed at WrestleMania 42, losing her Women's Intercontinental Championship to Becky Lynch. Yet, despite not appearing since that contest in Las Vegas, Lee is not retired from the squared circle.

Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select reported "sources that Fightful Select speak to believe she hasn't had her last match."

Addressing speculation that Lee would join forces with Paige to battle the Bella Twins, Sapp added: "Those in creative we spoke to said that they had not heard AJ Lee was actually planned for that angle and the talent involved hadn't been told what the plan was as of Brie Bella's injury."

Lee returned to widespread fan support and excitement last September and, aside from a match with Bayley, worked almost exclusively with Lynch. With a deep roster of Superstars she has rarely interacted with—let alone faced in the ring—Lee has plenty of fresh opponents.

When and where a potential return to the squared circle would take place remains a mystery, but Sapp's report is encouraging for fans who still want to see more of the revolutionary and inspirational Superstar.

When asked during Fightful Select Answers Q&A if Thekla was being saved for a potential debut by Kairi Sane at AEW All In, Sapp noted that as of August 21, "Kairi isn't signed to any company, and there's still work to be done on that."

Sane last appeared on WWE TV on the April 20 episode of Raw, teaming with Asuka in a losing effort against Rhea Ripley and Iyo Sky.

Sane was part of WWE's roster cuts this past spring, despite being heavily involved in an ongoing storyline with Asuka, in which it appeared she would eventually stand up to and feud with her tag team partner.

A great professional wrestler, Sane would give the women's division in AEW an even bigger boost, conceivably entering the title picture immediately. A match with Thekla would be outstanding, but time will tell if that is in the cards for both women.

In The Daily Update portion of F4WOnline.com, Dave Meltzer reported that, "Bayley was backstage at the TNA show yesterday. Between all the mentions last week on Raw and the callout by Blake Monroe, it would certainly seem like Bayley is not leaving WWE."

Lyra Valkyria has mentioned Bayley every week since defeating her and leaving her lying at Saturday Night's Main Event in July. Given WWE's continued on-air references to Bayley, it appears unlikely the company would keep featuring her name if it expected her to leave.

Still, it has been less about promoting The Role Model and more about putting over Valkyria's success and claim to the Women's Intercontinental Championship. Whether the long-running star of the women's division sticks with the company that helped make her a star remains to be seen.

Regardless of where Bayley ends up, the women's division will be better off for having her.

Bayley has been one of the most influential performers of her generation, and her impact on women's wrestling should extend beyond her in-ring career. Her Lodestone Wrestling initiative reflects her effort to help develop the industry's future.

articles.title: Santa Fe eliminó a River Plate: la millonada que ha ganado en Conmebol en 2026
articles.standfirst: El millonario premio que se aseguró Santa Fe tras eliminar a River
articles.summary: El millonario premio que se aseguró Santa Fe tras eliminar a River
articles.body: Independiente Santa Fe protagonizó una de las gestas más memorables del fútbol sudamericano reciente tras eliminar a River Plate en los octavos de final de la Copa Sudamericana 2026. Tras empatar 0-0 en la ida disputada en El Campín y firmar un dramático 1-1 en los 90 minutos de vuelta en el Estadio Monumental, el conjunto cardenal selló su boleto a los cuartos de final mediante una infartante tanda de penaltis (8-7 a favor de los colombianos). El compromiso de vuelta en Núñez tuvo momentos de alta tensión: Sebastián Driussi adelantó a los locales al minuto 52, pero el uruguayo Franco Fagúndez igualó las acciones de penalti al minuto 81, forzando una maratónica serie desde los doce pasos (22 cobros en total) donde la serenidad del equipo dirigido por Pablo Repetto terminó imponiéndose. Más allá del valor deportivo de situarse entre los ocho mejores clubes de la competición (donde se medirá ante Vasco da Gama), el triunfo representa un alivio sustancial para las arcas de la institución capitalina. Por haber clasificado a la ronda de cuartos de final, la Conmebol le otorgó al club un cheque directo de USD 700.000. Esta cifra se suma a un botín continental en 2026 que ya supera los 5.48 millones de dólares, producto de su recorrido internacional combinando su participación inicial en la fase de grupos de la Copa Libertadores y su posterior trasvase a la Copa Sudamericana. El acumulado financiero de Santa Fe podría seguir creciendo de forma significativa en las próximas semanas. Si el cuadro bogotano logra superar la llave de cuartos de final frente a Vasco da Gama y avanzar a las semifinales de la Copa Sudamericana 2026, asegurará un premio adicional de USD 800.000, afianzando un año extraordinario tanto en lo deportivo como en lo corporativo.

articles.title: La hazaña de Weimar Asprilla: Del banquillo a eliminar a River Plate anotando el penal decisivo
articles.standfirst: Weimar Asprilla, figura de Santa Fe vs. River Plate: Así fue la histórica clasificación en Copa Sudamericana
articles.summary: Weimar Asprilla, figura de Santa Fe vs. River Plate: Así fue la histórica clasificación en Copa Sudamericana
articles.body: La historia del fútbol sudamericano volvió a escribir uno de sus capítulos más épicos en la Copa Sudamericana. Independiente Santa Fe selló una clasificación inolvidable a los cuartos de final en pleno Estadio Más Monumental de Buenos Aires, y lo hizo con un protagonista imprevisto: el guardameta chocoano Weimar Asprilla. El portero de 27 años, quien asumió la titularidad de emergencia tras la lesión del referente Andrés Mosquera Marmolejo, pasó de ser la gran incógnita del partido a convertirse en la gran figura de la noche argentina. Tras el encuentro de ida en Bogotá y un reñido 1-1 en los 90 minutos de la vuelta en Argentina, la clasificación debió resolverse desde los doce pasos. La serie estuvo cargada de dramatismo, con intervenciones clave por parte del portero local Santiago Beltrán y cobros de alta factura de ambos planteles. El quiebre para el equipo bogotano llegó en la quinta ejecución de la tanda. Asprilla le atajó el penal decisivo al defensor Facundo González, manteniendo con vida las aspiraciones del conjunto cardenal y estirando la definición al "mata a mata". La tanda se prolongó hasta el undécimo tiro, instancia donde le tocó el turno a los porteros: Con la palabra "Fe" estampada en su camiseta con el número 12, el arquero originario de Quibdó celebró junto a sus compañeros un boleto histórico que regresa a Santa Fe a la élite del torneo continental. Tras concretarse el triunfo y desatarse la locura en la capital colombiana, el arquero dejó ver una camiseta de fondo con una cita bíblica: "Jehová es bueno, fortaleza en el día de angustia y conoce a los que en él confían", evidenciando la fe con la que afrontó este trascendental choque. En sus declaraciones posteriores al encuentro, Asprilla no dudó en atribuir su rendimiento a su convicción espiritual: "Lo único que les puedo decir es que esto es gracias a Dios, que sea la honra y la gloria para él. Dios me dio una palabra de que hoy iba a estar aquí, que él me iba a guiar y así fue, así que quiero darle la honra y la gloria a él", afirmó emocionado ante los micrófonos de la transmisión oficial. Además de su entrega y devoción, el guardameta tuvo palabras de reconocimiento para sus compañeros y de agradecimiento especial para un histórico de la institución: Robinson 'Rufay' Zapata, actual integrante del cuerpo técnico encabezado por Pablo Repetto y campeón con el club de la Sudamericana en 2015. "Agradecerle al grupo porque sin ellos tampoco hubiera sido posible. Esto es todo para 'Rufay' Zapata, que es un grande, que ya conoce este torneo y que nos ha trabajado muy bien", reconoció Asprilla.

articles.title: Se fuga un luchador egipcio tras los Juegos Mediterráneos en Taranto
articles.standfirst: El Comité Olímpico de Egipto suspende al jefe de la delegación de lucha, Ibrahim Adel, por "inacción y negligencia"
articles.summary: El Comité Olímpico de Egipto suspende al jefe de la delegación de lucha, Ibrahim Adel, por "inacción y negligencia"
articles.body: El Comité Olímpico de Egipto ha suspendido al jefe de la delegación de lucha, Ibrahim Adel, por "inacción y negligencia" después de que el luchador Mohamed Mustafa Ali al Shami "escapara" durante el tránsito en Roma hacia El Cairo tras participar en los Juegos Mediterráneos de Taranto (Italia). El comité anunció este jueves la suspensión en un comunicado, en el que explicó que, tras aterrizar su vuelo procedente de Taranto, el luchador "escapó durante el tránsito de la delegación de lucha en Roma durante su viaje de regreso a El Cairo tras el final de las competiciones de los Juegos Mediterráneos", que se celebran hasta el 3 de septiembre. Las investigaciones iniciales del organismo concluyeron que hubo "inacción y negligencia" por parte del jefe de la delegación y de su equipo, ya que el encargado debía estar en posesión de los pasaportes y documentos de viaje de los deportistas, pero ese no fue el caso. "Cuando el entrenador del deportista se dio cuenta de su desaparición, intentó localizarlo sin éxito. El entrenador se vio obligado a perder su vuelo de conexión, mientras que el luchador logró escapar", añadió el comunicado. El Comité Olímpico de Egipto justificó su decisión al explicar que "la fuga del deportista es una decisión individual, pero la supervisión de los miembros de la misión es una responsabilidad administrativa", mientras que indicó que la medida no es definitiva y que está sujeta a revisión, de acuerdo con la normativa. Esto se conoce días después de un incidente similar, en el que el luchador egipcio Ziad Hajaj abandonó la residencia del conjunto nacional en Eslovaquia tras participar en el Campeonato Mundial Juvenil de Lucha, de acuerdo con medios del país norteafricano. Varios deportistas egipcios han hecho lo propio en los últimos años, en medio de quejas por la falta de apoyo económico, la imposibilidad de poder vivir del deporte en Egipto, las restricciones a la hora de poder viajar debido a la dureza de los controles fronterizos, o la imposibilidad de salir del país sin haber hecho el servicio militar. De hecho, la premiada película egipcia 'Voy! Voy! Voy!' (2023), basada en hechos reales, relata la historia de un guardia de seguridad de El Cairo que finge ser ciego para poder participar en un campeonato internacional de fútbol para atletas con discapacidades, con la intención de escapar a Europa.

articles.title: La gran incógnita de Alcaraz
articles.standfirst: Para William Hill es el favorito a ganar el US Open, pese a llegar sin competir tras una grave lesión
articles.summary: Para William Hill es el favorito a ganar el US Open, pese a llegar sin competir tras una grave lesión
articles.body: El US Open arranca esta semana en Flushing Meadows envuelto en una de las incógnitas más llamativas de la temporada. Carlos Alcaraz llega como defensor del título, pero también como una auténtica incógnita física y de forma tras más de cuatro meses y medio sin competir por una seria lesión de muñeca. Pese a ello, y pese a la ausencia de Jannik Sinner, las casas de apuestas como William Hill mantienen al murciano como máximo favorito del cuadro masculino, una decisión que refleja más la confianza en su techo de nivel que las sensaciones mostradas en sus primeros entrenamientos en Nueva York. Y es que, esas sensaciones no han sido precisamente tranquilizadoras para su afición. Alcaraz ha disputado dos sets de entrenamiento estos días previos al torneo, cayendo por 7-5 ante Dani Mérida y, de forma más contundente, por 1-6 y 2-3 frente a Arthur Fils, recién campeón del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati. articles.title: La Federación Internacional de Pelota Vasca vuelve a denunciar la capitalidad mundial de Pamplona
articles.standfirst: La FIPV considera que el ayuntamiento de la capital navarra hace un uso indebido del lema ‘Pamplona Capital Mundial de la Pelota Vasca’, enmarcado su proyecto de la Agenda Urbana 2030, ya que lo hace sin su consentimiento
articles.summary: La FIPV considera que el ayuntamiento de la capital navarra hace un uso indebido del lema ‘Pamplona Capital Mundial de la Pelota Vasca’, enmarcado su proyecto de la Agenda Urbana 2030, ya que lo hace sin su consentimiento
articles.body: El Ayuntamiento de Pamplona presentó el pasado mes de enero su ‘Capitalidad Mundial de la Pelota’, una apuesta en clave turística que aprovechaba la historia y la cohesión social que genera este deporte en la región. De esta forma, ‘Pamplona Capital Mundial de la Pelota Vasca’ se convirtió en un proyecto estratégico, incluido en la Agenda Urbana 2030 de la ciudad. De hecho, a finales de octubre se celebrará un Congreso Internacional de Pelota Vasca en Pamplona para posicionar a la ciudad como epicentro de este deporte. Este proyecto de la capital navarra que gira en torno a la pelota no cuenta con el respaldo de la Federación Internacional de Pelota Vasca (FIPV), cuya Junta Directiva decidió en abril trasladar su sede social desde Pamplona, donde había permanecido los últimos 24 años, hasta Biarritz (Francia). Desde la FIPV se considera que se está usando de forma indebida el nombre de la campaña, algo que viene reiterando desde que la misma se presentó. La FIPV ha insistido hoy en su rechazo al uso de dicho lema a través de un comunicado y se emplaza a un diálogo entre las partes para resolver la situación. En el comunicado se explica que nunca hubo una consulta con la FIPV: “El pasado mes de enero esta Federación se pronunció públicamente para desvincularse de la denominación ‘Pamplona, Capital Mundial de la Pelota’, impulsada por el Ayuntamiento de Pamplona y presentada en el marco de FITUR. Así, al tener una connotación de naturaleza internacional o ‘mundial’ y al no haberse consultado con el resto de agentes integrantes de la comunidad, se declaró dicha denominación como carente de reconocimiento deportivo internacional”. En la Internacional, denuncian que un proyecto que además sigue creciendo ni siquiera se les haya consultado: “Han transcurrido varios meses desde entonces y esta Federación ha constatado que el citado proyecto, enmarcado en la Agenda Urbana Pamplona 2030, continúa desarrollándose y ampliando su alcance —incluyendo acciones tales como la organización de un congreso internacional, la construcción de un centro de interpretación de la Pelota Vasca o la constitución de una oficina internacional de prensa—. Ello, sin que se haya producido, hasta la fecha, un proceso de consulta, coordinación o validación con esta Federación”, prosigue el comunicado. La FIPV recalca que, según diversos artículos de sus estatutos, ella es “el único exponente de autoridad competente para todas aquellas iniciativas, proyectos, programas o acciones de naturaleza internacional vinculados a la Pelota Vasca”, pues todas estas iniciativas y su ejecución “inciden directamente en la imagen, la unidad y la representación institucional de la Pelota Vasca ante la comunidad deportiva internacional”. En la FIPV no dudan de que todos lo que abarca el proyecto de Pamplona es “de naturaleza indudablemente internacional, lo que conlleva que la participación y aprobación por nuestra parte sea cuanto menos exigible de cara a garantizar su legitimidad”. En cualquier caso, la Internacional quiere dejar “constancia expresa de que esta reivindicación no nace de una voluntad de confrontación, sino de la necesidad de preservar un marco ordenado, coherente y respetuoso con las federaciones afiliadas y con la propia esencia de un deporte”. En definitiva, el mensaje de la FIPV al Ayuntamiento de Pamplona es el de iniciar un diálogo para resolver la cuestión, como explica en la parte final del comunicado: “Esta Federación reitera su disposición a establecer un diálogo institucional con el Ayuntamiento de Pamplona y con cuantas entidades impulsan proyectos de esta naturaleza, con el fin de que cualquier iniciativa vinculada a la proyección internacional de la Pelota Vasca se desarrolle de forma coordinada, consensuada y conforme a los cauces estatutarios correspondientes. La colaboración leal entre las instituciones locales y esta Federación es, precisamente, la vía que permitirá dar a estos proyectos la legitimidad y el respaldo internacional que por sí solos no pueden alcanzar”. “En consecuencia, la FIPV emplaza a las instituciones promotoras del proyecto 'Pamplona, Capital Mundial de la Pelota' para que tomen en cuenta la legítima y exigible autoridad que esta Federación ostenta de forma competencial y redefinan sus objetivos y acciones limitándose a su ámbito competencial. Por otro lado, se invita a tales entidades promotoras para que acudan a esta Federación en propuesta de aquellas iniciativas de repercusión internacional para su debate y posterior decisión, toda vez que tal aprobación es competencia indiscutible de la FIPV”.

articles.title: Sri Lanka salvage draw in second Test after battling Dinusha denies India
articles.summary: Dinusha’s 133 not out, his second century of the match and third in four innings, helps the hosts avoid defeat.
articles.body:
Sri Lanka’s middle-order batter Sonal Dinusha engineered a remarkable rearguard action to help the hosts salvage a draw and deny India a series sweep in the second Test.

Dinusha made a stellar 133 not out, his second hundred of the match and third in four innings, to power Sri Lanka to 429-9 on Thursday while following on when the players shook hands.

India won the series 1-0 but Sri Lanka will take a lot of heart from their fightback at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground in Colombo.

Player-of-the-match Dinusha forged a century-run stand with Keshara Nuwantha to frustrate India and stayed put to help snatch a memorable draw.

Earlier, Sri Lanka resumed the final day of the rain-plagued match just 16 ahead and with only four wickets in hand.

They needed to bat out of their skin to save the test match, and Dinusha and Nuwantha (46) did exactly that, denying India success throughout the morning session.

Dinusha’s maiden Test hundred had been the bedrock of Sri Lanka’s first-innings total of 290, and the 25-year-old followed it up with his fourth successive score of 50 or more to keep his side alive in the contest.

Frustration grew in the Indian camp as Dinusha and Nuwantha put together a defiant 112-run stand, leading a spirited resistance.

Nuwantha also found himself on the right side of the review system twice, including in the final over before lunch, when he successfully overturned an lbw decision.

Spinner Manav Suthar finally broke the partnership in the first over after the interval. His delivery bounced and kissed the shoulder of Nuwantha’s bat before carrying through to Dhruv Jurel at slip.

Jurel then took a second catch to dismiss Prabath Jayasuriya for two, but Dinusha remained unperturbed despite being left to bat with the tail.

Lahiru Kumara provided invaluable support down the order, absorbing 90 balls for his dour 12.

On a pitch offering little assistance to the seamers, Dinusha defended with assurance and swept with panache to continue defying India.

Touring captain Shubman Gill rotated his bowlers and continually adjusted his field settings but nothing appeared capable of unsettling Dinusha, who batted with tremendous discipline.

articles.title: What did Victor Hedman reveal about leaving Tampa Bay Lightning before NHL playoff games against Montreal Canadiens

articles.body: Victor Hedman’s decision to walk away from the Tampa Bay Lightning late in the 2025-26 season has received a clearer explanation during the NHL offseason. The veteran defenseman recently spoke publicly about the physical issues and performance anxiety that kept him out, including Tampa Bay’s first-round Stanley Cup Playoffs series versus the Montreal Canadiens. His remarks also brought up the issue of mental health in pro hockey.Victor Hedman is leaving the Tampa Bay Lightning, saying he needs to focus on his mental and physical health following a difficult stretch. Six days later, Tampa Bay announced he was taking a leave of absence for personal reasons. did Victor Hedman leave Tampa Bay Lightning?“For me, it was not really feeling low, but it was performance anxiety, kind of feeling that pressure in your chest as soon as a game day would hit,” Hedman said. “It kind of locks you up. You make a mistake and in the past you’d be able to shake it off, but I couldn’t do that. And I wasn’t feeling 100 per cent physically.The news came after a season in which the 35-year-old defenseman was plagued by injuries. Hedman missed a lot of time with an elbow injury that required surgery, and then got hurt during warmups with Team Sweden before the 2026 Winter Olympics quarterfinal against the United States. articles.title: New NHL Rumors Reveal Cale Makar 'Closing In' on Contract Extension with Avalanche
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche reportedly aren't risking heading into the 2026-27 season with Cale Makar on an expiring contract.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche reportedly aren't risking heading into the 2026-27 season with Cale Makar on an expiring contract.

The Avalanche are "closing in" on an extension for Makar, according to Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman.

The most lucrative contract for an NHL defenseman is currently held by the Chicago Blackhawks' Bowen Byram, who signed his own record six-year, $75 million extension in July.

Makar, a two-time Norris Trophy winner who helped lead the Avs to the 2022 Stanley Cup, could potentially surpass that $12.5 million AAV after his sixth straight point-per-game season.

The news comes days after Avalanche president of hockey operations Joe Sakic told reporters he was "pretty confident [Makar]'ll be signed before the season starts."

"I'm not worried about it. I don't think Cale's worried about it," Sakic said, per NHL.com .

"Dialogue has been great and when there's an agreement, we'll gladly announce it. Hopefully something will be done before the start of training camp."

The Avalanche are expected to open training camp Sept. 17, per Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette. The NHL regular season kicks off Sept. 29, followed by the Avs' season opener Sept. 30.

Makar, who will turn 28 in October, was originally selected by the Avs with the No. 4 pick of the 2017 draft.

He has developed into one of the NHL's top defensemen during his seven seasons in Colorado, most recently ranking third among blueliners with 79 points (20 goals, 59 assists) in 75 games last season.

Makar also plays a key special teams role for the Avalanche, including on a penalty kill that ranked top in the league last season with an 84.6 percent success rate.

The Avalanche already have star center Nathan MacKinnon signed to a long-term contract alongside forwards Martin Necas and Logan O'Connor as well as defensemen Devon Toews and Brett Kulak.

With goaltender Mackenzie Blackwood also under contract until 2030, the Avs will hope locking in Makar to this core can help the team compete for another Stanley Cup after last season's conference finals elimination.

articles.title: Career turning point: “I cried a lot and threw my rackets everywhere”: How one emotional loss changed Roger Federer’s mindset and set him on the path to greatness
articles.summary: International Sports News: It is difficult to picture Roger Federer as the teenager he once was. The player remembered for his composure and elegant tennis spent his early years.
articles.body: It is difficult to picture Roger Federer as the teenager he once was. The player remembered for his composure and elegant tennis spent his early years struggling to control his emotions on court. Federer later admitted, “I cried a lot and I threw my rackets everywhere,” while reflecting on how badly he handled losses. His talent was never the issue. The bigger challenge was learning how to stop frustration from taking control of his game.The wake-up call came in Hamburg in 2001. Federer lost 6-3, 6-4 to Franco Squillari in the opening round of the Hamburg Masters, and the defeat stayed with him for a reason that had little to do with the result. He smashed his racket, cried over his performance and realized that his behavior could not continue if he wanted to reach the level he believed was possible. After years, Federer described the match as a key moment in changing the way he approached tennis.Why did the Hamburg defeat force Roger Federer to confront himself?Federer was already becoming a serious prospect in 2001. He had won his first ATP title in Milan earlier that year and was climbing the rankings, but his emotional reactions could still derail him when matches became difficult. A missed shot was sometimes followed by frustration, and that frustration could carry into the next point.The Hamburg loss brought the problem into focus. Federer later recalled reaching match point before Squillari hit a passing shot after he came toward the net. Federer went for the volley but could not immediately see where the ball had gone. He then realized it had become trapped between his racket and the court, ending the match. His reaction was to smash his racket while crying over how badly he felt he had played.Federer later recalled telling himself, “I can’t take this attitude.” He began thinking about what would happen if he continued behaving that way for another decade and realized he would not be able to cope. From that point, he decided he needed to become calmer and more concentrated.However, that didn't happen suddenly. Federer later explained that he initially went too far in the opposite direction, becoming so quiet that he appeared less competitive. He had to find a balance between what he described as “anger and calmness.”Did Roger Federer’s new mindset immediately make him a star?No, but the difference began appearing soon afterward. Just weeks after the Hamburg defeat, Federer arrived at Wimbledon and faced Pete Sampras in the fourth round. Sampras had won Wimbledon seven times and had not lost there in 31 consecutive matches, while Federer was only 19 and was playing on Centre Court for the first time.Federer stayed composed through a five-set battle and defeated the defending champion 7-6, 5-7, 6-4, 6-7, 7-5. He later admitted that his behavior had previously been a problem, saying, “I realised that the racquet throwing didn't help my game because I was always getting very negative.” He also explained that he had started relaxing more on court and was no longer smashing as many rackets.Federer still lost to Tim Henman in the quarterfinals, so the Sampras victory did not suddenly turn him into a champion. What it did was show that the young Swiss player could handle the biggest stage and compete with the best player of his generation.The two matches also tell an important part of the same story. Hamburg forced Federer to confront his behaviour, while Wimbledon gave him an early chance to see what he could achieve with greater control.When did Roger Federer’s mindset change become visible in his results?Roger Federer continued developing during 2002, winning the Hamburg Masters and breaking into the top 10. His game was becoming more complete, but the mental work that began after the Squillari loss was happening alongside those improvements.The breakthrough came at Wimbledon in 2003. Federer had never reached a Grand Slam final, but he beat Andy Roddick in the semifinals before defeating Mark Philippoussis 7-6, 6-2, 7-6 to win his first major title.His reaction afterwards was emotional, but for an entirely different reason. Roger Federer cried after finally winning the title he had dreamed about. He had not become emotionless. Instead, he had learned how to keep his emotions from interfering while the match was still being played.That distinction became an interesting factor when we remember his amazing transformation. Federer did not suddenly stop caring about losing, and he never became a player without emotion. He simply became better at separating what he felt from what he needed to do next.How did controlling his emotions shape Roger Federer’s career?By 2004, Federer had become world No. 1 and won three Grand Slam titles in the same season. The pressure had changed completely. He was no longer the young player trying to prove that he belonged. He was now the player everyone wanted to beat.His improved temperament gave his extraordinary tennis more consistency. Federer could lose a set without allowing frustration to ruin the next one, and he became increasingly comfortable staying patient when an opponent pushed him into difficult situations.The numbers that followed were extraordinary. Federer finished with 20 Grand Slam singles titles, including eight Wimbledon championships, and spent 310 weeks as world No. 1.Those achievements are usually linked to his serve, forehand movement and remarkable variety, but his emotional development was an important part of the same journey. The talent was already there. He needed to learn how to consistently access it under pressure.Thus, the Hamburg defeat deserves to be remembered as a genuine career turning point. It was not a Grand Slam victory or a famous upset, and it did not make Federer a champion overnight. Instead, it forced a gifted 19-year-old to recognise that his temperament could hold him back if he did not address it.Federer later described his younger self as someone who cried, threw rackets and struggled badly with losing. The player who eventually became one of tennis’s greatest champions was built through the process of changing that behaviour, not by pretending those emotions never existed.He learned that controlling his emotions did not mean caring less about winning. It meant giving himself a better chance to win.The teen who left Hamburg frustrated with himself could not have known what was coming. Within weeks, he would defeat Sampras at Wimbledon. Two years later, he would win his first Grand Slam there. By 2004, he would be the world's No. 1 player.The Hamburg loss did not create Roger Federer by itself, but it forced him to confront a weakness that could have followed him throughout his career. His greatest transformation began when he understood that before he could consistently control matches, he first had to learn how to control himself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
