articles.title: Tottenham sign Man City’s Egypt forward Omar Marmoush on season-long loan
articles.summary: Deal includes an obligation to make the move permanent next year, reportedly for a ⁠guaranteed $68m.
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur have signed ‌ Omar Marmoush from Manchester City on a season-long loan, the Premier League club ⁠has said, ⁠with the deal including an obligation to make the Egypt forward’s move permanent at the end of the season.

British media said the obligation to buy is for a ⁠guaranteed 50 million pounds ($68m), with 10 million pounds more in add-ons.

“It feels amazing to be here. I’m so excited to get started with the team, and I can’t wait to meet the ⁠fans,” the 27-year-old said in a statement released on Thursday.

“Tottenham Hotspur is one of the biggest clubs in England, if not the world, and the project was very attractive to me.

“I’ve spoken with the head coach [Roberto De Zerbi], I loved what he had to say, and I’m ‌sure our passion for the game will go very well together.”

Marmoush had a tale of two seasons at City, impressing in his debut 2024-25 campaign before finding consistent playing time elusive behind established players, including leading striker Erling Haaland, in Pep Guardiola’s squad last season.

He scored only three goals in 21 Premier League matches for City last term, a far cry from the seven goals in his first ⁠half-season at the Etihad Stadium.

De Zerbi, who took over at ⁠Spurs in March and helped them avoid relegation, wanted to add forwards to a rebuilt squad after they added midfielders Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes plus defender Jan Paul van Hecke for a combined 237 million pounds ($322m).

Spurs ⁠have also signed Brazilian winger Savio , formerly known as Savinho, from City in a deal reportedly worth about 75 million pounds ($102m) and ⁠a further 10 million pounds in add-ons.

Marmoush is a versatile forward ⁠capable of playing centrally or from the left wing, with the Egyptian expected to receive more playing opportunities under De Zerbi at Tottenham.

Spurs have needed more attacking quality after two difficult seasons in which they finished a lowly 17th in both.

Marmoush represented Egypt at the 2026 World Cup, playing five games, albeit without scoring, as they reached the last 16 before being eliminated by ‌eventual ‌runners-up Argentina.

Tottenham got off to a terrible start in their Premier League opener with a 3-0 drubbing at Brentford. They next host Newcastle United on Saturday.

articles.standfirst: Susto en el suroccidente de Colombia por temblor en la mañana: esto reportó el Servicio Geológico
articles.summary: Susto en el suroccidente de Colombia por temblor en la mañana: esto reportó el Servicio Geológico
articles.body: Un fuerte movimiento telúrico sorprendió a los habitantes de la capital del Valle del Cauca y de varias regiones del suroccidente de Colombia durante la mañana de este jueves 27 de agosto de 2026.De acuerdo con el informe oficial emitido por el Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC), el sismo se registró exactamente a las 10:25 a. m. (hora local), marcando una magnitud de 4,4 en la escala de Richter y situando su epicentro en el municipio de Istmina, en el departamento del Chocó. A pesar de que el epicentro se ubicó en la región del Pacífico chocoano, la profundidad de 43 kilómetros permitió que las ondas sísmicas se propagaran con fuerza hacia los valles y cordilleras vecinas. En Cali, así como en varios municipios del Valle del Cauca y el Eje Cafetero, los habitantes reportaron haber sentido un remezón rápido pero moderadamente intenso en pisos altos de edificaciones, oficinas y viviendas. Colombia es un país con alta actividad tectónica debido a la interacción continua de la placa de Nazca, la placa del Caribe y la placa Sudamericana. El litoral Pacífico y sus zonas de influencia —como el Chocó y el Valle del Cauca— son áreas de monitoreo permanente por la convergencia de estas fallas tectónicas. Tras la sacudida, las autoridades locales y los organismos de socorro (Cuerpo de Bomberos y la Gestión del Riesgo) iniciaron los barreos preventivos habituales en la infraestructura crítica de la ciudad y municipios cercanos. Hasta el momento del reporte preliminar, no se registraron daños materiales de consideración ni personas lesionadas. El Servicio Geológico Colombiano recuerda a la ciudadanía mantener la calma ante estos eventos y reportar su percepción a través de la plataforma oficial ¿Sintió este sismo?, herramienta clave para consolidar la intensidad percibida en cada territorio.

articles.title: WWE's ultimate what-if! Brock Lesnar vs Batista: Two powerhouses who arrived together, became world champions and never met in the ring - The blockbuster Vince McMahon never made
articles.summary: WWE News: Batista vs Brock Lesnar remains one of WWE's biggest missed opportunities.On paper, the matchup had everything Vince McMahon could have wanted. Two po.
articles.body: Batista vs Brock Lesnar remains one of WWE's biggest missed opportunities.On paper, the matchup had everything Vince McMahon could have wanted. Two powerhouse performers, two future world champions, two wrestlers who entered WWE around the same time. Yet despite their careers repeatedly crossing paths, Lesnar and Batista never shared the ring in a singles match.Both men joined WWE in 2000 and were sent to Ohio Valley Wrestling, then the company's developmental territory. They made their main-roster debuts in 2002, though WWE took them in very different directions from there.Lesnar was pushed as a once-in-a-generation athlete almost immediately. Batista took a slower route, building towards becoming one of the most important members of Evolution.Timing, departures and a string of creative decisions meant the collision never came, even when their paths seemed destined to cross at the peak of both careers.2000-2004: Two future stars arriveLesnar and Batista arrived in WWE at roughly the same time and quickly showed why the company viewed them as major prospects.Lesnar's rise was spectacular. He won the 2002 King of the Ring, then defeated The Rock at SummerSlam to become the youngest WWE Champion in history at just 25.Batista's journey was more gradual. He became the muscle of Evolution, standing alongside Triple H, Ric Flair and Randy Orton, and that role helped him develop into a major singles star and eventually put him on the path towards a world championship.Two enormous attractions, developing on separate tracks. A Lesnar-Batista match was almost impossible not to imagine.2004-2010: Lesnar leaves as Batista takes overThe first major obstacle arrived in 2004. After WrestleMania 20, Lesnar left WWE, a decision shaped by the demands of the company's travel schedule and his desire to pursue other interests.His departure came just as he appeared destined to become one of WWE's defining stars.The company did not have to look far for another powerhouse to fill some of that void. Batista continued his rise and won the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 21, going on to become one of WWE's biggest attractions with major programmes against Triple H, The Undertaker, Edge and John Cena.For years, Batista faced virtually every major name on the roster. There was just one obvious exception. Brock Lesnar.Batista left WWE in 2010, closing another chapter of his wrestling career. Then came the development that made the hypothetical matchup even more intriguing.Lesnar had moved into mixed martial arts and become UFC heavyweight champion. By the time he returned to WWE, he was no longer simply a former WWE champion, he was a legitimate combat-sports superstar.Batista also explored mixed martial arts during his own time away, though he never came close to Lesnar's level of success in the sport. That shared connection only made the idea of Batista vs Lesnar more appealing.Both were huge athletes. Both had become legitimate main-event attractions. Both had experience outside professional wrestling. WWE still had to wait for the right opportunity.2012-2014: The biggest missed opportunityLesnar made his shocking return the night after WrestleMania 28, attacking John Cena. From that point on, WWE treated him as a special attraction, used sparingly and against the biggest names available, including Cena and Triple H.Then, in January 2014, Batista returned. He won the Royal Rumble and earned a place in the WrestleMania 30 main event, challenging for the WWE World Championship.This was arguably the clearest window WWE ever had to make the match happen. The company could have built towards Lesnar winning the title and Batista challenging him at WrestleMania. Instead, it went in another direction entirely, putting Batista into a Triple Threat match against Randy Orton and Daniel Bryan.That decision produced one of WrestleMania's most memorable moments. It also meant another opportunity for Lesnar and Batista passed by.Lesnar, for his part, defeated The Undertaker at WrestleMania 30, ending his legendary 21-0 WrestleMania streak. Fans can only wonder, in hindsight, what might have happened had WWE chosen a different route.2014-2019: Lesnar dominates while Batista moves to HollywoodFollowing WrestleMania 30, Lesnar became one of the most dominant performers of his generation. He destroyed John Cena at SummerSlam, captured more world championships, and established himself as someone WWE could build an entire major event around.Batista, meanwhile, increasingly focused on his acting career. His role as Drax in Guardians of the Galaxy turned him into a Hollywood name, and wrestling was no longer his priority.The two men continued to exist in completely different worlds.2019: Batista's final chapterBatista returned to WWE in 2019 for one final major programme, this time with Triple H. The two faced each other in a No Holds Barred match at WrestleMania 35, which Batista lost before retiring from professional wrestling.It was a fitting ending to a career that included four World Heavyweight Championship reigns, two WWE Championship reigns and Royal Rumble victories in 2005 and 2014.One name was still missing from his list of major opponents. Lesnar.2026: Lesnar's retirement Lesnar's own career has now reached its conclusion. The 49-year-old recently confirmed on The Pat McAfee Show that his appearance at WWE SummerSlam against Oba Femi would be the final match of his professional wrestling career.Lesnar said he had felt he was finished earlier in the year at WrestleMania, when he removed his boots and gloves in the ring, but ultimately decided to have one final Hell in a Cell match in Minneapolis.His career closes with an extraordinary list of achievements. Lesnar became a 12-time world champion, winning seven WWE/WWE World Championships and three Universal Championships. He remains the youngest wrestler to win the WWE Championship, a feat he achieved at SummerSlam 2002 at 25.He also won the 2002 King of the Ring, the 2003 and 2022 Royal Rumbles and the 2019 Money in the Bank match. Most famously, he ended The Undertaker's 21-0 WrestleMania streak in 2014.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck Addresses NHL Trade Rumors Amid Sabres Buzz Ahead of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck has requested a trade from the Winnipeg Jets.
articles.body:
Three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck has requested a trade from the Winnipeg Jets.

Hellbuyck confirmed the news in a statement shared Friday by agent Ray Petkau.

"Several months ago, I privately requested a trade. I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options," Hellbuyck wrote.

"With training camp approaching, I felt it was important to publicly confirm my request. My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family."

Jets general manager Kevin Chevaldayoff released a statement in response to Hellebuyck, saying they will "continue to work through the situation in a thoughtful manner" but have "no update at this time."

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported ahead of the 2026 NHL draft in June the Jets were believed to have discussed a trade that would have sent Hellebuyck to the Buffalo Sabres.

Friedman reported at the time he believed Hellebuyck would have been willing to waive his no-movement clause in order to join the Sabres.

Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff declined when asked in June to clarify if Hellebuyck had asked for a trade, but said the team had "frank conversations" with the goaltender in end-of-season meetings.

Hellebuyck, who turned 33 in May, is signed through his age-37 campaign in 2030-31 on an $8.5 million AAV contract. His deal includes a full no-trade through next season, per PuckPedia .

After winning consecutive Vezina Trophies, Hellebuyck posted a career-low .895 save percentage for a Jets team that went 35-35-12 and missed the playoffs last season.

Hellebuyck seemingly expressed some doubt as to whether the Jets could turn things around next season in a postseason exit interview .

After he was asked about his future with the Jets, Hellebuyck said his career goal was to win a Stanley Cup and he was "just looking at how I can get that."

"It's hard. Can you get the pieces you need? Will the players come? These are always questions that you have in Winnipeg," Hellebuyck said in April. "I've made it my home, and I like it here, but I think majority of the league doesn't feel the same way."

Hellebuyck was selected by the Jets in the fifth round of the 2022 draft. He has played for the organization in all 11 seasons of his NHL career, during which he backstopped the Jets to a 2018 conference finals appearance and was celebrated as the league's top goaltender in 2020, 2024 and 2025.

Hellebuyck is the latest star from the American team that won gold at the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics to express interest in getting traded from a struggling team a contender.

Team USA star and former Vancouver Canucks captain Quinn Hughes was traded to the Minnesota Wild shortly before the Olympics, while former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk was dealt to the Florida Panthers in the following months.

Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin has also submitted a trade request, which his organization has yet to fulfill.

Hellebuyck could now hope publicly confirming his own request will put pressure on the Jets to move him before training camp starts next month.

If the Jets are interested in getting a starting goaltender back in a potential trade with the Sabres by targeting Ukko-Pekka Luukonen, Hellebuyck isn't the only one who would have to be interested in a move. Luukonen holds a five-team no-trade list through next season, per PuckPedia .

articles.title: Abbas gives Pakistan edge with four wickets against England in second Test
articles.summary: England battled back from 80-4 at lunch to 248-9 by the end of the rain-shortened first day at Lord’s.
articles.body:
Pakistan bowler ‌Mohammad Abbas took four wickets as his side edged the first day of the second ⁠Test against England at ⁠Lord’s Cricket Ground in London, although the hosts battled back from a rocky start to end a weather-shortened day on 248-9.

After Pakistan won the toss and elected to bowl on a ⁠muggy Thursday morning following a rain delay, Abbas took full advantage of the conditions to wreck England’s top order.

A stunning spell of three for 34 before lunch, including the removal of England captain Joe Root, put ⁠Pakistan in command, with the hosts reeling on 80-4 at lunch.

But England, led by half-centuries for Jordan Cox and Jamie Smith, responded to move towards a respectable total, especially against a Pakistan side whose batting was ruthlessly exposed in a heavy defeat at Leeds.

Cox dug in for 55 while Smith made an aggressive 61 as England ‌recovered from 120-5. Gus Atkinson swung the bat late on for an unbeaten 34 before bad light forced an early close.

The vastly experienced Abbas would have smiled when captain Babar Azam, back after missing the first Test defeat, called right to win a delayed toss.

Eight years ago at Lord’s, Abbas claimed eight wickets in a Pakistan victory, and he found conditions to his liking again as he went about his business in skilful fashion.

He made the breakthrough with the last ball of his third ⁠over when Emilio Gay tried to flick a leg-side ball off his ⁠pads but was caught by a diving Mohammad Rizwan behind the stumps.

Ben Duckett looked to be aggressive, but was undone when on 17 as Abbas jagged a ball back that trapped him on his back foot. He was given out leg before wicket (LBW) on review.

Root ⁠was dropped on one, but did not make Pakistan pay as he was trapped plumb LBW by Abbas.

Harry Brook was next to go, bowled by a ⁠peach of an inswinger by Mohammad Ali as England limped to ⁠lunch.

Cox, batting calmly at three, was joined by Dan Lawrence and they were digging in until Lawrence set off for a risky single and was run out by Rizwan after some sharp fielding by Shan Masood.

It took an extraordinary slip catch by substitute fielder ‌and former captain Salman Agha to remove Cox, clinging on one-handed to an edged drive off Khurram Shahzad.

Smith was looking dangerous but fell to Ali, who then bowled Ollie Robinson two balls later for a duck.

Abbas ‌took ‌his fourth wicket as Jofra Archer slogged across the line after making 14, but Atkinson was still there swinging as England repaired some of the earlier damage in the murk.

images.caption: A stunning spell of three for 34 before lunch put ⁠Pakistan in command of the cricket match, with the hosts reeling on 80-4 at lunch [Matthew Childs/Action Images via Reuters]

articles.title: Exequiel Palacios completes Ipswich switch
articles.summary: After six and a half years at Bayer Leverkusen, Exequiel Palacios is leaving the club to join Ipswich Town.Die Werkself confirmed the Argentina international...
articles.body:
After six and a half years at Bayer Leverkusen , Exequiel Palacios is leaving the club to join Ipswich Town.

Die Werkself confirmed the Argentina international's permanent transfer to the English Premier League side on Thursday evening.

"With this transfer, we are fulfilling Exequiel Palacios' great desire to test himself in the Premier League after his outstanding spell in the Bundesliga," said Bayer 04 sporting managing director Simon Rolfes .

"Pala has repeatedly demonstrated his excellent footballing ability and, through his character and attitude, has earned great respect from his teammates and everyone at the club. We wish him all the very best for his time in England."

Palacios made 186 appearances for Leverkusen, scoring 15 goals and providing 17 assists, and is grateful for his time at the club.

"I grew into the footballer I am today at Bayer 04. The club trusted me here, and I was able to develop everything that defines me on the pitch today," said Palacios.

"I will always remain connected to the boys, all the staff and the fans, and I will be firmly cheering Bayer 04 on during their matches. Thank you for everything, and thank you to a great club."

articles.title: Brandon McCoy Jr. injury casts a pall over Michigan's Europe finale
articles.summary: Michigan basketball ended its foreign tour on a bittersweet note.
articles.body:
Michigan basketball ended its foreign tour on a bittersweet note.

After dropping the first two exhibitions against Lithuania teams, the Wolverines capped their Europe trip with an 84-81 win over Serbia's Mega Superbet on Aug. 27 at the Sportski Centar in Herceg Novi, Montenegro but lost one of their standout freshmen in the process.

Brandon McCoy Jr., a five-star guard and one of the team's two incoming McDonald's All-Americans, exited 20 seconds into the game with an injury. After McCoy came away with a steal on the first possession, he slipped as he drove to the basket in transition.

McCoy stayed down for several moments and was tended to by trainer Chris Williams. He got up favoring his right leg and didn't put any weight on it before he was carried off the court and back to the locker room. He never returned to the bench.

The program didn't provide an immediate postgame update on McCoy's injury.

McCoy's exit overshadowed a contest in which Michigan trailed 49-38 at halftime and by three after the third quarter before it opened the fourth quarter with a 15-2 burst fueled by Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney. That put Michigan in front for good, though it had to hang on and stave off a late push by Mega Superbet.

The Wolverines were bit by the injury bug throughout their trip. Moustapha Thiam, the team's starting center, exited in the first quarter of Michigan's first exhibition game after his lower right leg was rolled up on by Cadeau. Thiam didn't play in the next two exhibitions.

Ricky Liburd was sidelined for all three games and McKenney didn't suit up for the second contest as they "rested nagging injuries as a precaution," according to a program release. Jalen Reed (Achilles) and Lincoln Cosby (ACL) were also unavailable as they continue to rehab and work their way back from their respective surgeries.

During its first leg of the 10-day trip, Michigan fell to the Lithuania national team, 96-84, on Aug. 23 and the country's reserve squad, 82-77, on Aug. 24 in Lithuania.

The Wolverines are scheduled to return to the United States on Aug. 29 and will look to heal up as they continue preparations for the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Will Kate Koval return to the Notre Dame Women’s Basketball team?

If you haven't heard by now, Kate Koval is leaving the LSU Tigers. The former Notre Dame women's basketball player was not happy that LSU Tigers head coach Kim Mulkey signed a Russian player, and 10 days after… Koval decided to leave.

With Koval's father being in the Ukrainian military and being part of the war aginst the Russian invasion — you can understand how she feels about all of this. Despite any offical statement from Koval on the matter, I think the reasons are fairly clear because it's all so personal.

We can debate about Kim Mulkey being… well, Kim Mulkey, at any other time, but right now I'm wondering where Koval might end up. Given the timing of everything, Koval won't be able to transfer and play this season and will have to wait until spring to decide where she will be going with the remaining three years of eligibility.

Is there a chance Koval returns to Notre Dame? To be honest, I don't quite remember the reasons for her departure from Niele Ivey's program, but she's a 6'5" center with two years of experience playing big girl basketball. They don't grow that on trees — so is there a chance?

articles.title: Minor League roundup, August 26: A 12-game winning streak for the (other) Giants
articles.summary: Yesterday on the farm.
articles.body:
And then there were 4. The season has officially ended for all 3 of the San Francisco Giants rookie ball teams. But the 4 A-ball Minor League Baseball affiliates are still in action. Here's what they did on Wednesday!

All listed positions in the roundup are the position played in that particular game.

Another draftee was given an assignment, as RHP Ian Korn, a 10th-round pick, was assigned to Low-A San Jose. Korn becomes the first pitcher from the Giants 2026 draft class to head to an affiliate. He's joined by RHP Jose T. Perez, who was promoted from the ACL.

RHP Sam Bower and LHP Hayden Wynja (who was rehabbing) were both moved from San Jose to High-A Eugene, while shortstop Kaeden Kent was activated by Eugene. Eugene infielder Zander Darby was sent to AAA Sacramento to fill in while the River Cats deal with an infield shortage.

Sacramento River Cats beat the Reno Aces (D-Backs) 6-4 Box score

It seems that LHP Cesar Perdomo is really adjusting to life in the Pacific Coast League. He's not dominating by any stretch of the imagination, but he's really figuring out how to get through games, which is pretty impressive given the offensive environment. Perdomo went 7 innings into Wednesday's game, which marked the 2nd game in a row in which he'd pitched 7 innings … and the 4th time in the last 5 games that he'd pitched at least 6.1. While the results weren't elite, they were solid enough, as the 24-year old southpaw gave up 8 hits, 3 walks, and 3 runs, while striking out 5.

In Perdomo's 1st 4 games with the River Cats, he pitched just 15.2 innings and gave up 15 earned runs; in 5 games since, he's thrown 32 innings with just 12 earned runs allowed. That's brought his ERA down to 5.10 and his FIP to 5.34, though he still has a low strikeout rate (6.8 per 9 innings, after being 11.1 in AA Richmond this year).

Perdomo, who signed in 2021 out of Venezuela, figures to be a very interesting Rule 5 decision this winter.

RHP Eric Cerantola had his 2nd straight dominant relief outing, retiring all 4 batters he faced, with 2 strikeouts. It was the 5th time in his last 6 appearances that Cerantola didn't allow a hit, and the 26-year old — who was claimed off of waivers, DFA'd, and outrighted this year — has been lights out for a while now. The 2021 5th-round pick walked 5 batters, all of which scored, in his 2nd outing with the organization. But in 10 outings since, he's thrown 12 innings and allowed just 5 hits, 3 walks, and 2 runs, with 17 strikeouts.

The offensive star was left fielder Will Brennan , who hit 2-5 with a home run, a double, and 3 runs batted in. Brennan's season has been more about contact than power — this was just his 6th home run, but he has a .316 average and a 10.7% strikeout rate — but the 28-year old veteran has done enough that he'll likely get an opportunity next season somewhere. He has an .803 OPS and a 109 wRC+.

Yet another strong game for center fielder Scott Bandura, who hit 2-5 with a double, a stolen base, and a strikeout. It's now an .898 OPS and a 135 wRC+ through 80 games for the just-turned 25-year old, with just a 14.8% strikeout rate and 22 swiped bags in 23 attempts. He looks more and more like a Rule 5 lock every day.

Right fielder Bo Davidson (No. 4 CPL) hit 2-5 with a strikeout, designated hitter Diego Velasquez (No. 31 CPL) went 1-2 with 2 walks, and catcher Adrián Sugastey hit 1-3 with a double and a sacrifice bunt. All 3 players have been very strong since their recent promotions to AAA.

Richmond Flying Squirrels lost to the Portland Sea Dogs (Red Sox) 5-4 (13 innings) Box score

Quite a funny game over in Virginia, where Richmond and Portland were tied 0-0 after 9 innings! They then took 4 extra innings to get things sorted out, scoring a run apiece in the 10th and 12th innings, before a combined 5 runs in the 13th and final frame.

Needless to say, the standouts were on the mound. Despite giving up 5 runs total (though just 2 earned, due to 3 being the Manfred Man), Richmond pitchers gave up just 6 hits and 2 walks in the 13 inning extravaganza. How impressive!

The biggest star on that front was LHP Esmerlin Vinicio, who made his 4th appearance since getting promoted. He was absolutely magnificent, pitching 3.1 no-hit innings with just 1 walk and 4 strikeouts. The 24-year old has allowed just 4 hits in 9 innings with the Squirrels, while striking out 10 batters. The lone ding has been that he's walked 7 batters.

RHP Shane Rademacher hasn't had the prettiest season, but he was very strong in this game, getting the start and throwing 3.2 shutout frames with just 2 hits and 1 walk allowed, while striking out 3. The 2023 undrafted free agent has a 4.22 ERA on the season, but a 6.18 FIP.

RHP Ryan Vanderhei retired all 6 batters he faced, with 1 strikeout, while throwing 15 of 23 pitches for strikes. The 25-year old, who was a 10th-round pick in 2023, has a 2.36 ERA since getting promoted, with a 4.16 FIP.

Not a lot on offense, as the Squirrels had just 9 hits in 13 innings, though they drew 8 walks. The best day belonged to second baseman Dayson Croes, who hit 3-5 and drew 2 walks. It's been a tough 2nd season of pro ball for the 26-year old lefty, who was returned to Richmond after a stint in Sacramento, and has hit worse in AA (.670 OPS, 82 wRC+) than he did in AAA (.728 OPS, 92 wRC+). Hopefully he can end the season strong.

Left fielder Jose Astudillo hit 2-6 and had a double, which was the only extra-base hit of the day for the Squirrels. He also stole a base and struck out once. Astudillo only has a .597 OPS and a 62 wRC+ with Richmond, but struggles are understandable given that A) it's a 9-game sample size, and B) he played just 15 games in High-A before getting promoted. The contact skills are translating, though, as he has just an 11.1% strikeout rate and an 8.5% swinging strike rate.

A tough day for center fielder Trevor Cohen (No. 15 CPL), who had an 0-7 which included 1 strikeout. Cohen, last year's 3rd-round pick, has really established himself as an awesome prospect this year, but has really cooled down following a strong introduction to the level. He has a .702 OPS and an 89 wRC+ in 35 games with Richmond.

Eugene Emeralds lost to the Everett AquaSox (Mariners) 11-6 Box score

Not a lot of good performances in this game, to be honest. It started on the mound, where LHP Henry Lalane had a tough go of it. The 22-year old, who was making just his 4th appearance with the Emeralds since coming over in the Heliot Ramos trade, made it through just 2 innings, and gave up 6 hits, which included a home run and 3 doubles. The 6'7 southpaw also walked 2 batters while getting tagged for 5 runs, and only striking out 1 batter.

Lalane is, without question, one of the top pitching prospects in the organization. He's also had a fair amount of struggles in High-A, though. After posting a 2.74 ERA and a 2.62 FIP, with 11.7 strikeouts per 9 innings in Low-A this season, Lalane has had just a 4.45 ERA, a 5.08 FIP, and 8.1 strikeouts per 9 innings in 7 starts in High-A, across the 2 organizations. He's a fairly intriguing Rule 5 decision, since he's a tantalizing talent, but does still seem to be quite a ways away.

RHP Matt Dunaway, a 27-year old in his 2nd season, also struggled mightily, as he gave up 6 baserunners and 4 runs in just 1.1 innings, though he did strike out 3. He has just a 5.53 ERA and a 5.10 FIP in Eugene this year, though his strikeout and walk numbers are solid (28 and 8, respectively, in 27.2 innings). RHP Alix Hernandez had the lone strong pitching performance, ceding 2 hits and 1 walk in 2.2 scoreless innings, while striking out 4. Hernandez, who just turned 22, has a 2.92 ERA but a 5.72 FIP in 12 appearances since getting promoted. Between Low and High-A this year, he has 75 strikeouts to 22 walks in 59.1 innings. There's something in that arm, that's for sure.

No real standout offensive days. The Emeralds only had 6 hits on the day, though 5 of them were doubles. Third baseman Walker Martin didn't get in on that action, as he went 0-1 with a strikeout and an error, but he did draw 3 walks and steal a base. It hasn't been a very good year for the 2023 2nd-rounder, who has just a .237 average, a .742 OPS, a 94 wRC+, a 32.9% strikeout rate, and 26 errors. But he's drawing a decent amount of walks (10.3% rate), stealing some bases (19 in 22 attempts), and showing off some power (.183 isolated slugging).

Right fielder Cam Maldonado (No. 34 CPL) had the only multi-hit day, as he went 2-4 with a double and 2 strikeouts. Maldonado, last year's 7th-round pick, has fit in quite well since a recent promotion. Despite having just an .825 OPS and a 100 wRC+ in Low-A this year, the righty has a .999 OPS and a 152 wRC+ through 14 High-A contests.

Shortstop Kaeden Kent, Jeff's son, who came over with Lalane in the Ramos trade, made his organizational debut and went 0-5 with a strikeout.

San Jose Giants beat the Visalia Rawhide (D-Backs) 12-6 Box score

It's a 12-game winning streak for the Baby Giants!

A so-so start for RHP Argenis Cayama (No. 13 CPL), who is hoping to end the year on a high note after missing a chunk of the season due to injury. Cayama showed off his brilliant stuff by striking out 6 batters in 4 innings, while allowing just 3 hits. But he was uncharacteristically lacking in control, as he walked 3 batters and hit another, en route to 4 runs.

Cayama hasn't had a great season — he has a 4.20 ERA and a 4.00 FIP — but my goodness is he an exciting arm. Despite still being just 19 years old, he has a brilliant 11.6 strikeouts and just 2.6 walks per 9 innings. He is someone worth being very excited about.

RHPs Dylan Carter and Melvin Pineda had phenomenal relief outings. Carter, a 25-year old UDFA from last year, pitched 2.2 perfect innings with 4 strikeouts, lowering his ERA to 4.99 and his FIP to 4.71, though he has just 8.9 strikeouts per 9 innings. Pineda, a 22-year old from Venezuela, retired all 3 batters he faced, with 2 strikeouts. He has just a 10.42 ERA and a 7.29 FIP in 15 games since getting promoted … but is striking out 11.8 batters per 9 innings, after K'ing a stunning 18.2 batters per 9 in the Complex League.

The star on offense was third baseman Dario Reynoso, who went 2-5 with a 2-run home run, his 4th of the season. Reynoso, a 21-year old from the DR, was hot earlier in the season, but was ice cold to start August. Through the first 10 games of the month, the righty hit just 4-37 with 0 home runs, 1 double, and 19 strikeouts. But he's been hot in 5 games since, hitting 8-24 with 2 homers and 2 doubles.

Reynoso still has a huge strikeout problem — he's K'ing at a 32.9% rate — but he has an .862 OPS and a 117 wRC+, with a .203 isolated slugging percentage. There's a lot to be excited about if he can harness the swings and misses.

Really nice games for center fielder Tanner Mally, left fielder Oliver Tejada, and second baseman Lorenzo Meola (No. 23 CPL). Mally, a just-turned 22-year old who was a 17th-round pick in July, hit 2-3 with a triple and 2 walks, giving him a 1.038 OPS and a 172 wRC+ through 16 pro games. What an introduction! Tejada, a 19-year old who was excellent in the Complex League this season, went 2-4 with a double, a walk, a stolen base, and a strikeout. He has a .739 OPS, an 84 wRC+, and 3 stolen bases in 36 games since getting promoted. Meola, last year's 4th-round selection, hit 2-4 with a triple, a walk, and a strikeout, boosting his OPS to .820 and his wRC+ to 103.

As for the other recent draftees, 5th-round designated hitter Luke Nixon had his best game, going 2-5 with 2 runs batted in, while 3rd-round outfielder Peyton Bonds didn't play. And quiet days for the superstars, as shortstop Josuar González (No. 2 CPL) went 1-5 with a stolen base and 3 strikeouts, while infielder Luis Hernández (No. 6 CPL) missed another game with an injury.

articles.title: Enzo Fernandez close to £120m Man City move after absence from Chelsea squad
articles.summary: The signing of Fernandez is set to take Manchester City’s outlay on midfielders this summer to around £300m
articles.body:
Manchester City are close to agreeing a £120m deal to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea .

The 25-year-old midfielder will become City's record signing if add-ons are met, but the base fee for the Argentina international is lower than the £116m fee City paid Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson earlier in the transfer window.

Fernandez was not in Chelsea 's squad to face Luton Town in the Carabao Cup , despite manager Xabi Alonso saying the previous day that he expected the midfielder to be involved, and he is set to be reunited with Enzo Maresca at the Etihad.

Fernandez has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City since the World Cup and Maresca's side were always expected to return with an offer for the Argentina international despite missing an informal deadline earlier this month.

It means City will have spent around £300m on midfielders this summer in what has been a complete overhaul following the departure of Pep Guardiola, whose exit was followed by those of Rodri and Bernardo Silva .

City have also recouped around £100m for selling Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Pro League club Al-Qadsiah and Nico Gonzalez to Newcastle. Maresca's side also added the signing of 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi for £86m following the arrival of Anderson.

The Independent understands Chelsea are prepared to go back to Bournemouth for midfielder Alex Scott after selling Fernandez. The Cherries have so far shut down any interest, but there's a belief a bid in excess of £80m, and probably closer to £90m, might bring reconsideration.

Alonso named a strong team to face Luton, selecting both Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers , but Fernandez was notably absent from the squad despite the new Chelsea manager saying he expected Fernandez to be included on Wednesday.

"We assessed situations, individual and collective and we have decided he is not in the squad for today," Alonso told Sky Sports before facing Luton, which was Chelsea's first competitive home game of the new season.

Fernandez featured off the bench for Chelsea in their Premier League opener at Fulham on Monday and was booed by the home fans at Craven Cottage for his role in the Argentina's World Cup semi-final win over England.

Fernandez received a comparatively warm reception from Chelsea supporters when he came on, having been previously booed during a friendly against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before the start of the season.

Asked whether he would like to keep Fernandez before the Luton match, Alonso added: "We want to have the best team possible. We know his qualities. He has shown it and we have to wait, but we will think about tomorrow and let's see how things develop."

articles.title: John Harbaugh Sends Clear Message to Cam Skattebo After Giants Practice Penalty
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has spent his first training camp with the team learning what makes running back Cam Skattebo tick. Skattebo returne...
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has spent his first training camp with the team learning what makes running back Cam Skattebo tick. Skattebo returned strong from a serious ankle injury in the Giants' 13-10 preseason loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and his energy has been a constant topic since.

This week, a reporter's question about that energy pulled a candid response out of Harbaugh.

John Harbaugh Calls Cam Skattebo's Energy "Infectious" In A Bad Way

During his media session Wednesday, Harbaugh was asked directly whether Cam Skattebo's energy is infectious for the rest of the Giants roster. The head coach did not hold back.

"Skatt's great. He does bring a lot of energy. But he did get a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice," Harbaugh explained . "Did you notice that? That's not infectious. Well, it is infectious, actually. Infectious in a bad way, right? Like infectious disease type of thing. We don't want that. So, we want it to be directed in a positive way."

The comment came after Skattebo slid following a reception and nearly took out the legs of a couple of Giants defensive backs during a non-contact drill.

Cornerback Greg Newsome and safety Jevon Holland were reportedly unhappy with the play, and the situation briefly escalated between the two sides. It marked the second time in recent practices that Skattebo's physical style drew a reaction from the defense, following an earlier collision with linebacker Zaire Barnes .

Harbaugh's message was clear. He wants Skattebo's competitive fire, just not at the expense of safety or team chemistry heading into the regular season.

Cam Skattebo's Rookie Season And Road Back

Cam Skattebo's competitive edge is exactly what made him a fan favorite as a rookie. He rushed for 410 yards and five touchdowns on 101 carries while adding 24 receptions for 207 yards and two more scores before a season-ending ankle injury against the Philadelphia Eagles cut his year short.

Skattebo has since opened up about his recovery , and general manager Joe Schoen confirmed the back was fully cleared for training camp. He carried the ball four times for 19 yards in the Giants' preseason opener against the Vikings and now sits atop the unofficial depth chart.

His off-field profile grew during the layoff too, including a memorable WWE appearance that had fans talking.

With roster cuts approaching and one preseason game left, all eyes turn to how Harbaugh handles his workload next.

The Giants sit 1-1 in the preseason after topping Miami 26-3 following the Vikings setback. They close out the exhibition slate Friday, August 28, hosting the Jets at MetLife Stadium before opening the regular season at home against the Dallas Cowboys .

articles.title: Center Nick Richards agrees to join Miami Heat on one-year deal
articles.summary: This isn't a surprise, the big man, entering his seventh NBA season, had been working out at the Heat facilities.
articles.body:
This was expected. Nick Richards had been working out in the Heat facility for a while, it was just a question of timing.

Now with the Klay Thompson signing complete, the Heat and Richards have come to terms on a one-year deal for Richards to be a backup center behind Bam Adebayo , the team announced Wednesday . This contract is not fully guaranteed until the season opens, notes Ira Winderman of the Sun-Sentinel . The Heat did the same thing a year ago with Precious Achiuwa , and it gives them flexibility if a player they are interested in becomes available.

Richardson will be the third center on the roster, playing behind Adebayo and Bobby Portis .

Richardson is a six-year NBA veteran, originally a second-round pick out of Kentucky. Last season, he split time between Phoenix and Chicago , appearing in 48 games and averaging 5.8 points and 5.1 rebounds per game.

This signing also puts the Heat at 14 standard contracts, which could be their roster heading into the season. They have the cap space to add a 15th player on a minimum contract, and veteran guard Gabe Vincent has been mentioned, but the Heat may choose to keep that roster spot open and see what develops. The non-guaranteed nature of Richardson's contract, and the fact that only $500,000 of Myron Gardner 's $2.6 million deal is guaranteed, gives the Heat flexibility.

The Heat also agreed to bring back Keshad Johnson on a two-way contract (he was on a standard contract with the team last season), Winderman reports.

articles.title: Rumour Mongering: Iraola Wants Three More Signings After Barcola
articles.summary: Tick-tock goes the clock.
articles.body:
Liverpool haven't yet completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain , though widespread reports over the last 24 hours have insisted his transfer is all but done with personal terms agreed and the two clubs putting the finishing touches on a package that could rise to £120M with add-ons.

Given the issues Liverpool came into the summer with on the squad front, though, and just how little they've managed to achieve with less than a week left in the transfer window, the question is whether Barcola might be the end of it. If he is, the Reds will be left recklessly short at multiple positions. Yet few on the outside would be confident of the club getting the necessary deals done.

However, setting aside larger doubts over the club's ability to execute successfully in the transfer market under sporting director Richard Hughes, fresh reports in the UK this evening suggest that more is at the very least the goal for the club in what's left of the summer window.

According to The Guardian's Andy Hunter , the club will still be pushing to sign a Mohamed Salah replacement right winger—though with left winger Barcola arriving as the star attacking signing, calling whatever player might end up being signed for the right the Salah replacement seems likely to apply more to position than to star power.

A second wing siging alongside Barcola was always expected, though. Less expected perhaps is the suggestion that new head coach Andoni Iraola wants to see his squad strengthened at right back given concerns over Conor Bradley 's long-term fitness as well as at striker given Hugo Ekitike is expected out until the new year.

"Ideally is the magic word," Iraola noted earlier in the day at his press conference ahead of Saturday's match against Nottingham Forest when pressed on the transfer issue. "We don't know what we can do, but now we have four or five days and I am sure if we can improve other areas we will."

In addition to depth concerns at right back and striker as well as the obvious need to sign another winger along with Barcola there are some question marks in midfield, particularly following the sale of Curtis Jones , but at the moment there has been no suggestion that the Reds are actively looking to make signings there.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins send Tutu Atwell to Rams for RB who just gained 68 yards
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins trade WR Tutu Atwell to the Rams for RB Jarquez Hunter.
articles.body:
Receiver Tutu Atwell 's homecoming in Miami didn't last long.

Atwell, signed by the Miami Dolphins in free agency to serve as a veteran in a receiving room packed with three rookie draft picks, was traded Aug. 27 back to the Los Angeles Rams , who sent the Dolphins running back Jarquez Hunter , a fourth-round pick in 2025 who appeared in only five games, playing only 22 snaps on special teams.

Photos: Miami Dolphins take on New York Giants in preseason game

Hunter is 5-feet-10 and 211 pounds, out of Auburn, where he led the SEC with a 6.4 yards per-carry average in 2024 while rushing for 1,201 yards.

The Rams traded Hunter despite a performance against the New Orleans Saints last week in which he rushed 12 times for 68 yards (5.7 average) and a 12-yard touchdown.

"Obviously, it was an awesome run by Jarquez Hunter to be able to get the last touchdown," coach Sean McVay said.

In Miami, Hunter is likely to get a look on special teams but could provide depth at running back behind De'Von Achane. The Dolphins addressed running back depth twice this week, having also signed Coleman Bennett.

There was a feeling on the part of Rams media that McVay was referring to Hunter this week when he described what he expects of any running back he'll send onto the field.

"Trust," he said. "That's the big thing. I've got to be able to trust that you can play without the ball, protect the quarterback, know where you're going to be in protections. It'll be hard for you to play for us if we don't trust you."

Atwell, originally a second-round pick of the Rams in 2021, had no catches in the preseason for the Dolphins and had little if any impact in training camp. He attended Miami's Northwestern High.

articles.title: Nine schools have multiple 5-star commits in the 2027 cycle
articles.summary: Once the five-star dominoes start to drop, they often fall in heaps. That was the case with the 32 best in the 2027 cycle. All 32 are already committed, as o...
articles.body:
Once the five-star dominoes start to drop, they often fall in heaps. That was the case with the 32 best in the 2027 cycle. All 32 are already committed, as of Aug. 27. A majority have been off the board for months with their recruitments shut down.

The old school recruiting timeline has vanished. The December signing period will, of course, come with its fair share of drama as flips and decommitments occur, but it's not as if there will be many fresh decisions to be made.

The 32 five-stars — according to the Rivals Industry Ranking — have dispersed among 16 schools. Nine of those schools have landed multiple. Rivals takes a look at those programs that reeled at least two big fish over the spring and summer:

OT Mark Matthews — No. 4 NATL. (No. 1 OT) S Kamarui Dorsey — No. 11 NATL. (No. 1 S) EDGE Zyron Forstall — No. 25 NATL. (No. 5 EDGE) IOL Kennedy Brown — No. 29 NATL. (No. 4 IOL) LB Kaden Henderson — No. 30 NATL. (No. 1 LB)

Mike Elko and the Aggies have the nation's No. 1 class, according to the Rivals Industry Team Recruiting Rankings. They've assembled an elite haul that currently features a quintet of five-stars, three of whom are the top-ranked prospects at their respective positions.

Dorsey has been in the mix since last November and his stock has soared since. The hard-hitting safety is also the No. 3 senior in Georgia. Forstall was next to follow at the end of March. The IMG Academy standout one of three A&M five-star commits who plays in Florida, alongside Matthews and Henderson.

Matthews ended a high-profile recruitment with a May decision, choosing the Aggies over Miami and plenty others. He's long been the top-ranked tackle in the cycle and forms an elite duo in the trenches alongside Brown, who committed in April and ranks as the No. 2 senior in the Lone Star State.

Then there's Henderson, who jumped in the mix during official visit season in June. What really makes A&M's class so stacked, though, is the additional six commits who rank inside the top 60 nationally. Cornerback Raylaun Henry and wide receiver Eric McFarland are both currently on the cusp of five-star status, too.

CB Donte Wright — No. 9 NATL. (No. 1 CB) CB A'mir Sears — No. 10 NATL. (No. 2 CB) WR Nick Lennear — No. 17 NATL. (No. 3 WR) EDGE Jaiden Bryant — No. 24 NATL. (No. 4 EDGE)

The Miami Hurricanes have formed the nation's No. 3 class this cycle. No coaching staff have pulled off bigger flips than Mario Cristobal and Co. as two of their four five-star pledges were previously committed elsewhere.

It starts with Wright, the top-ranked senior in California. The Long Beach Poly playmaker made a very early commitment to Georgia, but Miami was among the many teams in pursuit throughout the spring. He flipped in May and has since shut down his recruitment and is also now the No. 4 prospect in the updated Rivals300.

Wright was then flanked by Sears at the end of July. Considered one of the top prospects in the 2028 cycle, Sears caught most off guard when he announced his decision to reclassify up to the senior cycle. He simultaneously set his commitment date with all arrows pointing toward Coral Gables. He's a two-way standout at the high school level and could try to play both sides at the next level.

Bryant was the other massive flip back at the beginning of June. The one-time LSU commit opted to flip after logging his official visit. He's the No. 1 overall prospect in South Carolina. Lennear was a classic Miami recruiting win. The in-state pass-catcher was trending toward The U for months before pulling the trigger on his commitment in March.

EDGE David Jacobs — No. 3 NATL. (No. 1 EDGE) WR Jamier Brown — No. 19 NATL. (No. 4 WR) DL Marcus Fakatou — No. 31 NATL. (No. 2 DL)

Ohio State now has the nation's No. 5 recruiting class in the nation and No. 2 class in the Big Ten heading into the fall. The Buckeyes' trio of five-star commits showcase how many different ways you can win a recruitment.

Brown is the best senior prospect in the state of Ohio. He was prioritized early by the OSU staff and made a very early commitment on Nov. 23, 2024. Despite the departure of longtime receivers coach Brian Hartline , Brown remains rock-solid.

Jacobs was a Miami lean heading into his Dec. 29 decision. It was known that Ohio State was still in the mix, but just minutes before he revealed his commitment, the Buckeyes overtook the Hurricanes and swiped one of the biggest pledges of the cycle. Making a switch like that would make one think that his recruitment would carry a few twists and turns down the stretch, but Jacobs has been rather quiet since coming off the board.

OSU then went out to the West Coast this summer to pluck Fakatou, the No. 3 senior prospect in the Golden State. He considered numerous high-profile programs and named multiple leaders throughout his recruitment, but the Buckeyes emerged as the team to beat leading into his June 29 commitment and they got over the finish line.

The Notre Dame class remains at No. 2 nationally thanks to three five-stars and five more top-100 overall prospects. The Fighting Irish also inked a top-two class in the previous cycle and continue to recruit at a truly elite level.

May was a massive month on the trail for Marcus Freeman and his staff. Olubobola pledged on May 12, choosing the Irish over a slew of blue bloods. The 6-foot-6, 300-pounder reminds Rivals' Scouting and Rankings Team of former Notre Dame star Ronnie Stanley .

Olubobola, the No. 1 senior in New Jersey, was a classic Notre Dame target. So was Sesay, the No. 3 prospect in Pennsylvania. The Downingtown East standout was trending toward South Bend for some time before locking his commitment during OV season.

Simien joined Olubobola in the trenches at the end of June. The No. 3 prospect in Louisiana spurned the usual SEC suitors and is headed for the Midwest. Notre Dame's class also features DL David Folorunsho , a five-star in the Rivals300 rankings.

articles.title: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town, League Cup: Post-match reaction, ratings
articles.summary: It was attack versus defense from minute one to minute last, though we were made to wait for a while for the Chelsea breakthrough. That breakthrough would ev...
articles.body:
It was attack versus defense from minute one to minute last, though we were made to wait for a while for the Chelsea breakthrough.

That breakthrough would eventually come from the simplest of plays: a nice cross from Malo Gusto putting the ball onto Danny Welbeck 's head, and the debutant making no mistake just as he had often done so in the colors of other teams at Stamford Bridge. Nice to see him scoring for us, for a change!

Chelsea had spent much of the first half trying to find intricate ways through the massed ranks of the visitors, but outside of the first 10-15 minutes, when we were a bit more willing to go more direct, we were not making much headway. When we did get into decent positions, Luton would inevitably block the shot. Morgan Rogers did hit the post, in fairness, at the end of a move that definitely deserved a goal, but otherwise it was a frustrating occasion for the first 45 minutes.

Welbeck's goal in the 50th minute didn't really change the flow of the game, with Luton simply hoping to keep it close until the late stages. Unfortunately for them, those late stages would bring a goal for Chelsea instead, with Barco winning the ball in midfield, Palmer feeding Estêvão , and the youngster forcing the own goal at the far post after losing his marker 1-v-1.

The job was done. We had a couple great chances to add to the scoreline, but it would stay at 2-0. In stoppage time alone, JP was denied from close range while Gittens hit the inside of the post but saw the shot unluckily bounce straight back out.

More of a back-four this time from Alonso, with Lacroix and Acheampong the central partnership and Gusto and Chavarria on the sides. Hato on for Gusto for the final 20+ with Acheampong moving wide right.

Full debuts for Penders, Welbeck, and Barco; and a debut goal for Welbeck!

Sadly, no debuts for Emegha or Watson off the bench

Early-season exuberant application of the one of the new rules from IFAB that's being implemented: substitutes have to leave the pitch in 10 seconds; if they don't, the sub cannot come on for a minute, or the next break in play, whichever occurs later. Welbeck apparently took too long and JP had to wait, with Chelsea down to ten for those two minutes.

We will be playing Leeds United at the Bridge in the third round in a couple weeks

articles.title: Blue Jays quietly sign ex-Phillies All-Star pitcher recently released by Rockies
articles.summary: Toronto has apparently signed an All-Star starting pitcher.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays have quietly signed a right-handed starting pitcher who earned an All-Star selection in 2023.

The Colorado Rockies recently released the 12-year veteran after he posted an ugly 7.08 ERA with a Major League-high 168 hits allowed in 25 starts.

MLB.com's Keegan Matheson reported on Thursday that Michael Lorenzen has signed a Major League contract with the Blue Jays.

"Michael Lorenzen has a locker in the #BlueJays ' clubhouse today," Matheson wrote on X. "Lorenzen was recently released by the Rockies."

Matheson reports that Lorenzen, 34, has a locker in Toronto's clubhouse.

Before today, there were no reports that the Blue Jays were interested in the right-hander, who signed a one-year, $8 million contract with the Rockies during the offseason.

"Although this year has been one to forget for Lorenzen, the former two-way player has a generally solid track record as a back-of-the-rotation starter. From 2022-25, he combined for 522 2/3 innings of 4.10 ERA ball between the Angels, Tigers, Phillies , Rangers and Royals," Steve Adams of MLB Trade Rumors wrote.

Toronto's rotation has been hit hard by injuries in 2026, and Shane Bieber recently hit the injured list due to shoulder inflammation.

If the Blue Jays advance to the postseason, their top two starters would almost undoubtedly be Dylan Cease and Jose Soriano.

articles.title: Tutu Atwell Reunion Protects Potential Rams Weak Spot
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams brought back wide receiver Tutu Atwell just months after he left, shoring up a position group of concern. The post Tutu Atwell Reunion P...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are bringing back a familiar face in a bid to increase their odds of success in a Super Bowl or bust season.

Tutu Atwell reunion with the Rams — Ava Brand (@avaonbrand) August 27, 2026

The Rams traded for wide receiver Tutu Atwell, who had just left for the Miami Dolphins in free agency this past March, in exchange for running back Jarquez Hunter , reports Adam Schefter, ESPN's NFL insider .

Why did the Rams bring back Tutu Atwell?

Atwell, who's spent all five of his NFL seasons with the Rams, returns at a key time for the team.

The Rams have Super Bowl aspirations, but one of their biggest weaknesses is depth at the wide receiver position.

Their stars, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , are excellent, but there's a good bit of uncertainty behind them, especially given Adams' injury history and Nacua's physical style of play, explained Los Angeles Sports Report's Nelson Espinal.

"There's a lot of questions at the pass catcher position once you go beyond the two stars at top, so I think that easily, when you look at the depth chart, receiver is the biggest question mark and the biggest weakness on this Rams roster," he said.

It's possible that Adams and Nacua could miss time. Adams hasn't played a full regular season since 2023, when he was with the Las Vegas Raiders .

And Nacua, who's dealing with a psoas injury this preseason , could also be suspended for a tumultuous offseason that included a trip to rehab , allegations that he bit a woman and reports of antisemitic comments and gestures .

If either or both of the wideouts misses playing time, having someone with experience in head coach Sean McVay's system will be important, as it's "notoriously super hard to understand," Espinal added.

"When you have two players like that with, I would say, very reasonable health question marks, it's going to really matter who your third pass catching option is," Espinal said. "And when you look at the receiver depth chart, it's pretty bare bones. You have a bunch of guys who I would say are more replacement level receivers, and then you have rookie CJ Daniels who could possibly take a big leap. But again, these McVay offenses, they're so hard to get a good hold of."

Given the risks involved in an all-in season, it makes sense while the Rams would return to the familiar.

Are you excited to see Tutu Atwell back on the Rams?

articles.title: White Sox gift Chicago native Pope Leo XIV a team-branded mitre
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox have given their most holy fan, Pope Leo XIV, an official White Sox mitre. Check it out here.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox are having a pretty magical season. Despite losing more than 100 games in each of the last three seasons, the ChiSox suddenly find themselves in first-place in the AL Central with fewer than 30 games remaining.

It amost feels like too quick a turnaround. This team would've needed multiple high-end acquisitions or multiple elite prospects to graduate. They've certainly had a few between Colson Montgomery , Braden Montgomery and Munetaka Murakami , but it didn't seem like that would be enough to turn around what has been a basement-dwelling franchise in just one year.

It's almost like ... they've been the beneficiaries of divine intervention.

On Thursday, Aug. 27, the team gave renowned fan and Chicago native Pope Leo XIV his own White Sox -branded mitre (the tall, ceremonial hat worn by the Pope), a solid offering to someone who perhaps was sending daily prayers to his favorite franchise.

articles.title: 30 Day Countdown – Day 8: Storyline We Will Become the Most Tired of This Year
articles.summary: Normally I try and lead articles with multiple potential options before I revealed my final choice, but there is a storyline that I am so tired of that I wan...
articles.body:
Normally I try and lead articles with multiple potential options before I revealed my final choice, but there is a storyline that I am so tired of that I want to get straight into it.

Technically it is a two parter, but the same core concept around QB Demond Williams. Is the team rallied around him after his transfer portal drama and can he take the next step to elevate the team. Most of us have heard these questions repeated ad nauseam at this point all offseason and unfortunately it will likely occur during the season as well.

Did Demond cause tension and drama among the fanbase? Yes. Did he ever lose the locker room afterwards? Not at all. That is backed up by every player on the team who has been asked about it.

Demond is a hard worker by all accounts of his coaches and we have no reason to doubt that he has been locked in. He had a bit of a shaky spring, but he was excellent in fall camp and looks ready to go for a big season ahead.

So who will call into question all of this? Every single member of the media. I predict after every bad series or error that Demond has the narrative will be similar, ""He can't be making these kinds of mistakes if he wants to take his team to the next level." It is so easy to condemn and so hard to create. People will fall back on that storyline as a crutch every time he does anything questionable or has less than an ideal outcome.

The team has moved on from it, so it's time for the fans and media to let it die in the offseason as well. Even though I know they won't.

articles.title: 'It gets very frustrating': Shubman Gill coming to terms with the captaincy challenge
articles.summary: With the series won and positives accumulated, Shubman Gill asserted that they still have a good chance to qualify for the WTC final. The Indian captain is h...
articles.body:
TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: In his first press conference of the tour, Shubman Gill termed qualifying for the World Test Championship as the "ultimate goal," a sentiment he maintained while preparing to leave the country. In between his two media interactions, the Indian captain saw his team register a comprehensive win in Galle and then settle for a draw in a fixture they were well positioned to win in Colombo. Although the series was won, the trophy secured, and his undefeated run as captain checked off crucial boxes, India left behind crucial WTC points needed to boost their win percentage. As captain, he had his most challenging few days under the sun in Colombo when Sonal Dinusha and the Sri Lanka's tail frustrated the visitors and prevented them from getting the result they desperately wanted. There were moments he would helplessly stand and observe from the short-cover position, have an intense chat with head coach Gautam Gambhir when nothing worked and then even egg his teammates on when their shoulders started dropping. "It gets very frustrating," he said regarding the challenges, explaining the questions that follow. "Was follow-on the best decision, was it not? But then you have to go back in the moment and see, what can I do? Did I make the best decision in that moment? Yes, I did. Then you can't do anything about it. You have to keep trying your best, and I think we did that," added the Indian captain. While they struggled to remove the Sri Lankan tail in both innings, Gill was not ready to pin the blame on any of his teammates and lauded their effort. "We tried all that we could, and at the end of the day, even from the players, you can expect them giving their 100%, their top efforts, and I don't think there was any lacking in intensity or the efforts that we put in," said Gill.

Highlighting the volume of overs the spinners bowled on a surface which became easier to bat as the game progressed, Gill gave them 10/10 for effort and intent, and continued to focus on the ultimate goal - the World Test Championship. "The spinners bowled 50-60 overs on the trot for three days. Fielding for three days is not an easy task in these conditions with the heat. In terms of effort, I would say 10 out of 10 for the effort and the intent. A lot of learning, so many things won't always go as you plan, but as long as we still have a chance to qualify for the World Test Championship," added Gill. India operated with in-out field positions for most of the match, offering significant protection against the sweep, especially when Sonal Dinusha was at the crease. While it did open up easy singles, Gill felt there couldn't have been a better plan as the slow turn off the surface meant bowled and LBW were the dismissals out of the equation. "The ball was spinning but the wickets were not in play. As a batsman, if you know that your bowlers do not have 2 modes of dismissal in play, then it becomes easier to bat. Unless you are playing shot and not looking to make a run, then it is difficult to take a wicket," said Gill.

"They were sweeping, step out and you also have to have your close-in fielders for the catch. So there was a lot of in-and-out field and there was always a lefty and a righty batting. So it's especially on a wicket like this it's difficult to have a field on one side," added Gill on his field placements. With the series won and positives accumulated, Gill asserted that they still have a good chance to qualify for the WTC final. The Indian captain is hopeful to do well in New Zealand and be in a better position by the time Australia come for the Border Gavaskar Trophy early next year. "I still think we've got a pretty good chance to qualify for the WTC. If we play the New Zealand series well and then hopefully, by the time the Australia series comes, we just have to win the series. If we're in a situation where we just have to win the series, I think we'll be in a good position to qualify for the WTC. A lot of solidity and a lot of confidence in our betting lineup, for sure. I always feel if you put up runs in test matches, three and a half, four sessions, you're always in the game. "We've got bowlers that can make up 20 wickets. As long as we keep putting 350-400 runs consistently on the board, we'll always be in the game and looking at our batting performances, it's very pleasing to see that we are doing that," said Gill. There is still time before India start preparing for their next Test assignment. For now, the immediate focus will be on recovering after the grind in Galle and Colombo, and then hoping the best pool of players are available when the selectors assemble to pick squads for the New Zealand tour.

articles.title: Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant explains why he's constantly firing back at hecklers
articles.summary: "I'm gonna hit you in the soul": In a 68-minute interview, Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant covered a lot of ground, including why he talks back to heckling...
articles.body:
Kevin Durant never minds getting into a verbal back-and-forth with anybody. The Houston Rockets star used to spend a lot of time interacting with fans - and plenty of haters - on social media, before he slowed down after the alleged Twitter burner account incident , but it doesn't sound like he'll ever stop the talking while on the court.

In an episode of Boardroom Talks , which posted online Thursday, Durant, who co-owns the sports, media and entertainment brand Boardroom , sat for a 68-minute interview with Speedy Morman, who pointed out to the future Hall of Famer that he's an easy target for fans to rage-bait.

"It's not rage-baiting when you're going to leave this interaction feeling f- up," Durant told him. "I'm gonna hit you in the soul. It's just real personal s-. Like 'I'm way better than you at life. I've accomplished what you want to do in life. You're watching me. You pay my rent.' All types of stuff. I go that far, because you don't need to talk to me like that. You can cheer for me and react to a player, but you want to see this side of me, so why not?"

Durant made the case that fans actually enjoy getting cursed at by the player they're yelling at on the court.

"It just feels like, 'That's why I bought my tickets to really get a feel for who these dudes are. I know they're not just the perfect individuals, we know we've got some crazy motherf- in our league, so let me see. Let me rage bait one of these dudes real quick,'" Durant said. "Sometimes dudes might ignore them, but now people know if they say something to me, I'm going to say something back."

Durant even had a snappy comeback about how he feels after the interaction.

"I feel great that I can provide them with one of their most core memories of their life. That simple," he said.

One thing Durant says he doesn't do is ask for security to eject a fan for talking trash. When he played for the Phoenix Suns , Durant had a viral interaction with a Dallas Mavericks fan , who called him an expletive before a game and when Durant turned back to talk to the fan, she switched up and tried to shake his hand. Durant explained that moment and said security at the Mavericks' arena asked if he would like the woman ejected and he declined.

"I don't like getting people kicked out when they just heckle me and s-, because I know I'm going to get buckets that night, so I know I'm just going to use y'all as a reason," Durant said.

The interview covered a lot of ground - no, he wasn't actually trying to hide behind a bush when he was eating at Nobu in Malibu this summer, and yes, he does take a shower most days , estimating he bathes 350 days a year - but also talked about his future, since he turns 38 in September and will be playing his 20th season in the league and second with the Rockets. He said the retirement of his former Oklahoma City Thunder teammate Russell Westbrook this summer hit home for him, but he sounded like he has more years left in him.

Notably, Durant, who averaged 26 points in his first season with the Rockets, has a player option to remain in Houston in 2027-28 for $46 million.

"It's a young man's game. Even though I feel like I can play, you are always hear, 'You're 38, you're 39. You're getting up there.' So, yeah, I get that, but I put everything into the game and I'm cool with whatever happens as I move forward," said Durant, who can pass Kobe Bryant for fourth place on the NBA's all-time scoring list this season. "I'm going to continue to put everything into the game until I can't no more."
